                  f"for these {len(targets)} blocks (${per_block:.4f}/block)")
            n_volume = volume_blocks * escalation_share
            scope = ("the blocks that would escalate across the volume"
                     if args.a_on_fail else "the whole Čechy volume")
            print(f"  extrapolated to {scope} (~{n_volume:,.0f} blocks): "
                  f"${per_block * n_volume:,.0f}, or "
                  f"${per_block * n_volume / 2:,.0f} on the Batches API")
            # The estimate above bills the system prompt at the cache-read rate on
            # all but the first call. That only happens if it clears the model's
            # minimum cacheable prefix — below it, caching fails silently and every
            # block pays the full input rate instead of a tenth.
            minimum = CACHE_MINIMUM.get(args.model)
            if minimum and est_cached < minimum:
                uncached = (est_in + est_cached) * rate_in + est_out * rate_out
                print(f"  ! the ~{est_cached}-token system prompt is under "
                      f"{args.model}'s {minimum}-token cache minimum, so it may not "
                      f"cache at all — worst case ${uncached / 1e6 * len(targets):.2f} "
                      f"for these blocks, ${uncached / 1e6 * volume_blocks:,.0f} for the volume. "
                      f"Check usage.cache_read_input_tokens on the real run.")
        else:
            reader = build_reader(args)
            print(f"  reader: {reader.name}")
            pages_cache: dict[str, tuple] = {}
            for stem in blocks_by_page:
                page = lx.read_alto(CZ_PAGES / f"{stem}.alto.xml")
                image = lx.render_page(CZ_PDF, int(stem), page.width)
                pages_cache[stem] = (page, image)

            # A CACHE FOR THE TABLE TOO (D-115), keyed like the notes' crop cache:
            # the tiles' bytes and captions, the instruction, the model, the prompt
            # and every thinking setting. It is what lets the table be batched: a
            # run with --batch-prepare queues each uncached block instead of
            # sending it, reader_batches.py writes the replies here, and the next
            # run reads every block from the cache.
            table_cache = None
            if not args.no_crop_cache:
                table_cache = (out_dir / "table_cache"
                               / (args.notes_label or "unlabelled"))
                table_cache.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            table_lock = threading.Lock()

            def table_key(parts, instruction: str) -> str:
                h = hashlib.sha256()
                for piece in ([encode_png(im) + "\0" + cap for im, cap in parts]
                              + [instruction, str(getattr(reader, "model", "")),
                                 str(getattr(reader, "system", "")),
                                 str(getattr(reader, "temperature", "")),
                                 str(getattr(reader, "reasoning_effort", "") or ""),
                                 str(getattr(reader, "thinking", "")),
                                 str(getattr(reader, "effort", ""))]):
                    h.update(piece.encode("utf-8"))
                    h.update(bytes(1))
                return h.hexdigest()

            def run(job):
                stem, block = job
                page, image = pages_cache[stem]
                tiles = lx.tile_block(image, page, block, template,
                                      tiles=args.tiles)
                parts, instruction = block_parts(tiles)
                key = table_key(parts, instruction) if table_cache else None
                hit = table_cache / f"{key}.json" if key else None
                if hit is not None and hit.exists():
                    record = json.loads(hit.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
                    return stem, block, record["lines"], record.get("usage", {})
                if args.batch_prepare and hit is not None:
                    make = getattr(reader, "params", None) or getattr(reader, "body", None)
                    if make is not None:
                        line = json.dumps({"key": key, "reader": reader.name,
                                           "cache_dir": str(table_cache),
                                           "slot": [stem, block.block_id], "kind": "table",
                                           "model": getattr(reader, "model", ""),
                                           "payload_key": getattr(reader, "payload_key", "rows"),
                                           "request": make(parts, instruction)})
                        with table_lock:
                            with open(args.batch_prepare, "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                                fh.write(line + "\n")
                        return stem, block, None, {"error": "batched: queued"}
                for attempt in range(3):
                    try:
                        rows, usage = reader(parts, instruction)
                        if hit is not None:
                            tmp = hit.with_suffix(".json.part")
                            tmp.write_text(json.dumps({"lines": rows, "usage": usage,
                                                       "slot": [stem, block.block_id],
                                                       "kind": "table",
                                                       "model": getattr(reader, "model", ""),
                                                       "at": time.time()}), encoding="utf-8")
                            tmp.replace(hit)
                        return stem, block, rows, usage
                    except Truncated:
                        # Not a transient fault: the same call will truncate again
                        # at the same cap. Raise the ceiling instead of sleeping.
                        if hasattr(reader, "max_tokens"):
                            reader.max_tokens = min(reader.max_tokens * 2, 32000)
                        if attempt == 2:
                            return stem, block, None, {"error": "truncated"}
                    except Exception as exc:            # noqa: BLE001
                        if attempt == 2:
                            return stem, block, None, {"error": str(exc)}
                        time.sleep(2 * (attempt + 1))

            started = time.time()
            with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=args.workers) as pool:
                results = list(pool.map(run, targets))
            elapsed = time.time() - started

            failures = 0
            for stem, block, rows, usage in results:
                for key in ("input", "output", "cache_write", "cache_read"):
                    usage_total[key] += usage.get(key, 0)
                if rows is None:
                    failures += 1
                    continue
                a_raw[block.block_id] = rows
                rebuilt = rows_to_block(stem, block.index, rows)
                if rebuilt is None:
                    failures += 1
                    continue
                a_blocks[block.block_id] = rebuilt
                for record in lx.grade_page([rebuilt]):
                    record["channel"] = "A"
                    record["block_id"] = block.block_id
                    records.append(record)
            print(f"  {len(a_blocks)} blocks transcribed, {failures} failed, "
                  f"{elapsed:.0f}s wall clock "
                  f"({elapsed / max(len(targets), 1):.1f}s/block)")
            print(f"  tokens: {usage_total['input']:,} in "
                  f"({usage_total['cache_read']:,} cache reads), "
                  f"{usage_total['output']:,} out")
            if args.reader == "claude":
                cost = (usage_total["input"] * rate_in
                        + usage_total["cache_write"] * rate_in * 1.25
                        + usage_total["cache_read"] * rate_in * 0.1
                        + usage_total["output"] * rate_out) / 1e6
            elif reader_price:
                # No caching on this path, so every token billed at the full input
                # rate — which is why a cheaper per-token rate need not be cheaper
                # per block.
                cost = (usage_total["input"] * reader_price[0]
                        + usage_total["output"] * reader_price[1]) / 1e6
            else:
                cost = None
            if cost is None:
                print("  cost: not priced — pass --reader-price IN,OUT to put this "
                      "reader on the same yardstick (a self-hosted reader is priced "
                      "by whoever runs it; compare on the pass rate and s/block)")
            else:
                per_block = cost / max(len(a_blocks), 1)
                print(f"  cost: ${cost:.2f}  (${per_block:.4f}/block, "
                      f"${per_block * volume_blocks:,.0f} for the volume)")
                if args.reader == "claude":
                    print(f"        ${per_block * volume_blocks / 2:,.0f} on the Batches API "
                          f"(50% off, no latency guarantee)")
                elif usage_total["input"]:
                    # The system prompt is resent in full on every block here. Say
                    # how much of the bill that is, since it is the part prompt
                    # caching would have removed.
                    print(f"        no prompt caching on this path: "
                          f"{usage_total['input']:,} input tokens billed in full")

            for block_id, rebuilt in a_blocks.items():
                stem = block_id.split("#")[0]
                original = next(b for b in blocks_by_page[stem]
                                if b.block_id == block_id)
                for finding in compare_channels(original, rebuilt, "AB_agree"):
                    finding["channel"] = "A|B"
                    records.append(finding)

    # ---- channel C ------------------------------------------------------- #
    if "C" in channels:          # free — runs under --dry-run too
        print("\nchannel C (German volume) ...")
        try:
            import pandas as pd
            import pdfplumber

            districts = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data" / "final" / "geo" / "districts_1910.csv")
            index = lxde.build_page_index(DE_TEXT)
            pdf = pdfplumber.open(DE_PDF)

            # Pair through the authority, not by comparing the two volumes' names
            # to each other: both sides are OCR, and the German scan is the worse of
            # the two ("Uo.jeschin" for Hojeschin). Each side is matched to a known
            # obec instead, and two blocks are the same municipality when they
            # anchored to the same one.
            okres_id_to_de = {}
            for row in districts.itertuples():
                code = str(row.okres_code)
                if "-" in code:
                    land_code, number = code.split("-")
                    okres_id_to_de[int(f"{land_code}{int(number):03d}")] = str(row.okres_de)

            grid = lxde.fit_grid(pdf, list(range(60, 260)))
            findings: list[dict] = []
            paired_total = 0
            de_anchor_rows: list[dict] = []
            for okres_id, anchors in sorted(cz_anchors.items()):
                okres_de = okres_id_to_de.get(okres_id)
                de_pages = lxde.okres_pages(index, okres_de) if okres_de else []
                if not de_pages:
                    print(f"  okres {okres_id} ({okres_de}): "
                          f"not located in the German volume")
                    continue
                german_blocks: list[lx.Block] = []
                for number in de_pages:
                    rows = lxde.extract_rows_de(pdf, number, grid)
                    blocks, _ = lx.segment_blocks(rows)
                    german_blocks += [b for b in blocks if not lxde.is_heading(b)]
                candidates = authority.okres(okres_id)
                de_anchors = lxnm.anchor_blocks(german_blocks, candidates)
                pairs = lxnm.pair_by_obec(anchors, de_anchors)
                paired_total += len(pairs)
                matched_de = sum(1 for a in de_anchors if a.verdict == "matched")
                print(f"  {okres_de}: German pages {de_pages}, "
                      f"{len(german_blocks)} de blocks, {matched_de} anchored, "
                      f"{len(pairs)} paired with a Czech block")
                for anchor in de_anchors:
                    de_anchor_rows.append({
                        "block_id": anchor.block_id, "okres_id": okres_id,
                        "printed_name": anchor.printed, "verdict": anchor.verdict,
                        "obec": anchor.obec.cs_name if anchor.obec else "",
                        "score": anchor.score, "runner_up": anchor.runner_up,
                    })
                cz_by_id = {b.block_id: b for bs in blocks_by_page.values()
                            for b in bs}
                de_by_id = {b.block_id: b for b in german_blocks}
                for obec, cz_anchor, de_anchor in pairs:
                    cz_block = cz_by_id.get(cz_anchor.block_id)
                    de_block = de_by_id.get(de_anchor.block_id)
                    if cz_block is None or de_block is None:
                        continue
                    for finding in lxde.compare_cells(cz_block, de_block):
                        finding["row_name"] = obec.cs_name
                        findings.append(finding)
            for finding in findings:
                finding["channel"] = "C|B"
            records += findings
            write_csv(out_dir / "anchors_de.csv", de_anchor_rows)
            print(lxde.lexikon_1910_de_report(grid, paired_total, findings))
        except Exception as exc:                        # noqa: BLE001
            print(f"  channel C failed: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")

    # ---- report ---------------------------------------------------------- #
    # Labelled with the pass, for the same reason its other artefacts are: two
    # readers over the same pages must not overwrite each other's ledger.
    checks_name = f"checks_{args.notes_label}.csv" if args.notes_label else "checks.csv"
    write_csv(out_dir / checks_name, records)
    rows_name = (f"table_rows_{args.notes_label}.csv" if args.notes_label
                 else "table_rows.csv")
    write_csv(out_dir / rows_name, table_rows(blocks_by_page, a_raw))
    print()
    for channel in ("B", "A"):
        subset = [r for r in records if r.get("channel") == channel]
        if subset:
            print(f"--- channel {channel} against the invariants "
                  f"({len(blocks_by_page) if channel == 'B' else len(a_blocks)} "
                  f"pages/blocks)")
            print(lx.lexikon_1910_report(subset))
            print()
    for label, title in (("A|B", "channel A vs channel B"),
                         ("C|B", "channel C vs channel B")):
        subset = [r for r in records if r.get("channel") == label]
        if subset:
            counts = Counter(r["verdict"] for r in subset)
            graded = counts["pass"] + counts["fail"] + counts["unparseable"]
            rate = f"{counts['pass'] / graded:.1%}" if graded else "--"
            print(f"--- {title}: {counts['pass']} agree, {counts['fail']} disagree, "
                  f"{counts['unparseable']} unreadable, {counts['na']} both blank "
                  f"-> {rate} agreement")
    print(f"\nper-check records written to {out_dir / checks_name}")
    print(f"per-page geometry written to {out_dir / 'geometry.csv'}")
    return 0

'You are transcribing one block of a printed statistical table from the 1910 Austrian census: *Podrobný seznam míst v Čechách* (Special Place Register for Bohemia), printed in Vienna in 1916 in Czech, in blackletter-era roman type.\n\nThe image shows one municipality (obec) and the settlements (osady) printed beneath it. Vertical rules separate the columns. The table has exactly 17 columns, in this left-to-right order:\n\n 1  seq              the running number in the leftmost narrow column\n 2  name             place name, often "Czech, German" together, sometimes with\n                     printed symbols and bracketed figures after it\n 3  area_ha          area in hectares — printed ONLY on the municipality line\n 4  houses           number of houses\n 5  pop_total        present population, together\n 6  pop_male         present population, male\n 7  pop_female       present population, female\n 8  conf_catholic    Roman Catholic\n 9  conf_evangelical Evangelical\n10  conf_israelite   Israelite\n11  conf_other       other or no confession\n12  lang_german      nationals by language of daily use: German\n13  lang_czech       nationals by language of daily use: Czech-Moravian-Slovak\n14  lang_other       nationals by language of daily use: other\n15  foreigners       foreign nationals\n16  post_key         postal delivery district — a footnote key such as "13)"\n17  station_note     nearest railway station and walking distance, e.g. "10) 2 1/4"\n\nRules:\n- Transcribe exactly what is printed. Do not correct, complete, infer, or compute\n  any value from any other value. If a figure is genuinely illegible, put "?" —\n  do not guess a plausible number.\n- A cell holding a centred dot "." is the printed nil marker. Return "" for it.\n  Return "" for a truly empty cell too. Never write "0" or "." for either.\n- The image is cropped to one block, but a sliver of the row above or below may be\n  visible at the very top or bottom edge. Ignore any partial row that is cut off.\n- Every printed line gets one object, in printed order, including any\n  "mezi tím vojsko" line.\n- Long place names wrap onto a second printed line; join them into one object.\n- Return the figures as digit strings, without thousands separators.\n'

"""Calibration run for the 1910 special place register — four channels, one grader.

Measures the pass rate and the cost *before* anything is committed to, on a source
with no gold standard. The channels read the same pages without being told what
the others said, and a deterministic grader that none of them can see scores the
result:

  B  the NDK ALTO text layer, snapped to the reconstructed grid   (free)
  G  the below-table apparatus, read from the image by an OCR
     model, returned as printed lines                             (billed, cheap)
  C  the German volume, located by running head, both sides
     anchored to settlements_1910 and paired on the shared obec   (free)
  A  a vision model on a crop of a municipality block             (billed, off by default)

**The spend is deliberately unequal, because the source is.** Between the printed
rules the ALTO reads digits at ~88%, and a second billed reading of a block that
already satisfies every arithmetic identity buys confirmation of what was not in
doubt. Below the rules it reads almost nothing worth having: the apparatus is
small type, superscript keys, and — for most of what it records — *pictograms*,
which no amount of parsing recovers from a text layer that never identified them.
So the default run reads the apparatus with a model and the table without one.
Channel A stays available for the blocks channel B failed (``--a-on-fail``), which
is the only place a per-municipality rate is worth paying.

The arithmetic is what makes that safe. The table has invariants; the apparatus
has none, so its guard is a **closed vocabulary**: the reader may name a symbol
only from the volume's own printed legend (*Výklad značek*, p. XI, carried in
``institution_abbreviations.csv``), and anything else is ``[?]``. A token off the
list is rejected on arrival and counted in the ledger rather than normalised away.

Channel G returns *printed lines*, not structure, so its output is assembled into
the same ``Notes`` object the ALTO produces and every downstream consumer — section
cutting, ``parts_check``, the postal legend, the institution decoder — runs on it
unchanged. That is what makes the two readings comparable instead of merely both
present.

Every block is also anchored against the municipalities its okres is known to
contain. That is the only check here that can see a block which should not exist,
or a municipality the parser lost — no arithmetic identity can.

The readers are the only model-specific part: everything downstream (grid, blocks,
invariants, anchoring, grader) is indifferent to which model produced the rows, so
a candidate reader can be scored on exactly the same yardstick.

**The model never sees the invariants.** It is asked to transcribe what is printed
and nothing else — no mention that the sexes sum to the total, that the confessions
sum to the total, or that the settlements sum to their municipality. A model told
what the numbers must add up to will return numbers that add up, and the pass rate
stops measuring anything. For the same reason a failing block is re-read, never
repaired: nothing that fails is quietly patched into the output.

Two local models, two different jobs
------------------------------------
Run against a local Ollama daemon, the reading costs nothing and the constraint
becomes wall-clock. It is worth splitting the work by what each model *is*:

* **A dedicated OCR model** (``glm-ocr``: 0.9B, of which the language side is a
  0.5B decoder) transcribes this print better than a general model its size, and
  cannot be asked to hold an 83-token taxonomy or a JSON schema while doing it. It
  gets ``--notes-style transcribe`` and ``--notes-format text``: every symbol comes
  back as ``[?]``, which still records the **position and the count** of each one,
  so the slots survive for a later pass.
* **A general vision-language model** (``qwen3.5``, 4b/9b) can hold the closed list
  and the schema, so it gets ``--notes-style annotate`` and is the one that can
  actually *name* a post office or a school.

Both defaults are inferred from the model id and announced. Run them as two
labelled passes over the same pages and compare: the ``[?]`` slots from the first
are exactly what the second has to fill, and both are graded against channel B by
the same arithmetic.

Why a section and not a column (``--notes-sections``)
----------------------------------------------------
The two passes above want different crops, and it took a failure to see it. A
footnote column is ~1,350 x 1,000 px of six-point type; ``glm-ocr`` reads it in
one call, and ``qwen3.5`` does not — on page 270 it returned the ``Části osad``
section and stopped, one line short of the ``Úřady`` heading and everything under
it. Halving the column changed the failure mode rather than fixing it: the
bottom halves came back well-formed and **empty**, which is worse, because a
region with no lines reads downstream as a part of the page that was blank.

So the crop is cut on the print instead. The register organises the apparatus
into sections — one heading, one soudní okres, one kind — and the ALTO already
knows where every heading sits, so ``--notes-sections offices`` sends each
``Úřady, ústavy`` section as its own image: a median of 478 px instead of a whole
column, 1.77 crops a page instead of 3, a prompt that describes one kind of entry
instead of five, and 56 symbol tokens instead of 83. What comes back is joined to
the text layer's own reading of the same sections per municipality entry
(``symbol_join_*.csv``), where the text layer supplies *where* every marker is and
the model supplies *which* one it is — and the entry is refused whole if the two
disagree on how many markers it has.

Finding the headings is load-bearing for all of it, and the rule that found them
was too narrow. It matched on the heading's first word, which is set in the
largest face on the page and is therefore the worst-read text on it — ``Úřady``
arrives as ``Hřady``, ``tířady``, ``TJřady``, ``Ĺ ř a d v .``. That lost **137 of
1,146 headings**, and a lost heading is not a lost section: its entries were
being attached to the previous heading, so one district's institutions were
filed under its neighbour's name. ``lexikon_1910_notes`` 0.4.0 anchors on the
tail instead (``okresu X:``) and classifies the kind from fragments that survive
the damage, which reproduces the old rule exactly on the 1,009 it found and
recovers the rest.

Usage
-----
    # everything free — no API key, no spend
    python utils/lexikon_1910/run_lexikon_1910_pilot.py --channels B,C

    # does the local model see the image at all, and how fast? run this first
    python utils/lexikon_1910/run_lexikon_1910_pilot.py --probe \
        --notes-reader ollama --notes-model glm-ocr

    # pass 1 — transcription by the OCR model
    python utils/lexikon_1910/run_lexikon_1910_pilot.py --pages 118-137 \
        --notes-reader ollama --notes-model glm-ocr --notes-label glmocr \
        --workers 1

    # pass 2 — the symbols, by a general vision model, over the same pages
    python utils/lexikon_1910/run_lexikon_1910_pilot.py --pages 118-137 \
        --notes-reader ollama --notes-model qwen3.5:9b --notes-label qwen \
        --workers 1

    # pass 2, targeted: only the Úřady, ústavy sections, each cut on its own
    # printed heading and sliced to 500 px. This is the pass to give a small
    # local model — see "Why a section and not a column" below
    python utils/lexikon_1910/run_lexikon_1910_pilot.py --pages 118-137 \
        --channels B,G --notes-sections offices --notes-max-height 500 \
        --notes-reader ollama --notes-model qwen3.5:9b --notes-label qwen \
        --workers 1

    # the same crops, a different reader — the only change is the model id and
    # the label, so the two land side by side and are graded identically
    python utils/lexikon_1910/run_lexikon_1910_pilot.py --pages 118-137 \
        --channels B,G --notes-sections offices --notes-max-height 500 \
        --notes-reader ollama --notes-model gemma4:12b --notes-label gemma \
        --workers 1

    # one crop first: does this model hold a whole section, and how fast?
    python utils/lexikon_1910/run_lexikon_1910_pilot.py --probe --probe-page 270 \
        --notes-sections offices --notes-reader ollama --notes-model qwen3.5:9b

    # the table as well, free: any reader can be scored on the same invariants
    python utils/lexikon_1910/run_lexikon_1910_pilot.py --channels B,A \
        --reader ollama --reader-model glm-ocr --a-on-fail

    # a hosted reader instead, priced so the comparison is a cost comparison
    python utils/lexikon_1910/run_lexikon_1910_pilot.py --channels G \
        --notes-reader glm --notes-model <model-id> --notes-price 0.6,1.8

    # only the postal/railway legend — the smallest crop, and where the text
    # layer is visibly worst
    python utils/lexikon_1910/run_lexikon_1910_pilot.py --channels G \
        --notes-reader ollama --notes-model glm-ocr --notes-regions footer

    # score a different reader on the same pages and the same yardstick
    python utils/lexikon_1910/run_lexikon_1910_pilot.py --channels A \
        --reader openai-compatible --reader-url http://localhost:8000/v1 \
        --reader-model <model-id>

    # GLM (Zhipu / Z.ai), which speaks the same OpenAI-compatible dialect.
    # --reader-price is what makes the comparison a *cost* comparison: the rate
    # is supplied rather than assumed, because only the Claude table is known here.
    python utils/lexikon_1910/run_lexikon_1910_pilot.py --channels A \
        --reader glm --reader-model <model-id> --reader-price 0.6,1.8

Choosing a channel-A reader
---------------------------
The reader is swappable precisely so the expensive one is not assumed to be
necessary. Channel B already establishes the floor these pages must beat, so the
question a candidate reader answers is not "is it good" but "does it clear 87.7%
on the same 308 blocks". Two things about a non-Claude reader change the
arithmetic and are handled rather than assumed:

* **No prompt caching.** The system prompt is billed in full on every block
  instead of at a tenth on all but the first, so a per-token rate that looks
  cheaper is not automatically cheaper per block. ``--reader-price`` prices it
  honestly.
* **Schema enforcement varies.** ``json_schema`` is requested, then degraded to
  ``json_object``, then dropped — a reader that cannot hold the schema should
  score as a worse reader, not crash the run and score as nothing.
"""

TRANSCRIBE_SYSTEM = """\
You are transcribing one block of a printed statistical table from the 1910 \
Austrian census: *Podrobný seznam míst v Čechách* (Special Place Register for \
Bohemia), printed in Vienna in 1916 in Czech, in blackletter-era roman type.

The image shows one municipality (obec) and the settlements (osady) printed \
beneath it. Vertical rules separate the columns. The table has exactly 17 columns, \
in this left-to-right order:

 1  seq              the running number in the leftmost narrow column
 2  name             place name, often "Czech, German" together, sometimes with
                     printed symbols and bracketed figures after it
 3  area_ha          area in hectares — printed ONLY on the municipality line
 4  houses           number of houses
 5  pop_total        present population, together
 6  pop_male         present population, male
 7  pop_female       present population, female
 8  conf_catholic    Roman Catholic
 9  conf_evangelical Evangelical
10  conf_israelite   Israelite
11  conf_other       other or no confession
12  lang_german      nationals by language of daily use: German
13  lang_czech       nationals by language of daily use: Czech-Moravian-Slovak
14  lang_other       nationals by language of daily use: other
15  foreigners       foreign nationals
16  post_key         postal delivery district — a footnote key such as "13)"
17  station_note     nearest railway station and walking distance, e.g. "10) 2 1/4"

Rules:
- Transcribe exactly what is printed. Do not correct, complete, infer, or compute
  any value from any other value. If a figure is genuinely illegible, put "?" —
  do not guess a plausible number.
- A cell holding a centred dot "." is the printed nil marker. Return "" for it.
  Return "" for a truly empty cell too. Never write "0" or "." for either.
- The image is cropped to one block, but a sliver of the row above or below may be
  visible at the very top or bottom edge. Ignore any partial row that is cut off.
- Every printed line gets one object, in printed order, including any
  "mezi tím vojsko" line.
- Long place names wrap onto a second printed line; join them into one object.
- Return the figures as digit strings, without thousands separators.
"""

ROW_SCHEMA = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
        "rows": {
            "type": "array",
            "items": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {c: {"type": "string"} for c in lx.COL_NAMES},
                "required": lx.COL_NAMES,
                "additionalProperties": False,
            },
        }
    },
    "required": ["rows"],
    "additionalProperties": False,
}


def encode_png(image) -> str:
    buffer = io.BytesIO()
    image.save(buffer, format="PNG")
    return base64.standard_b64encode(buffer.getvalue()).decode("ascii")


class Truncated(RuntimeError):
    """The reply hit ``max_tokens``. Distinct because the fix is a bigger cap."""


class RateLimited(RuntimeError):
    """The endpoint refused because a quota is spent, not because it failed.

    Distinct from every other error for one reason: **retrying is the wrong
    response and the ordinary retry path does it anyway.** A crop that raises is
    retried three times with 2 s and 4 s between, which is right for a dropped
    connection and useless against a limit measured in minutes or hours — it just
    spends three requests to learn the same thing, and each of those may itself
    count against the quota.

    It also has to be distinguishable *downstream*, and that is the more important
    half. On a plain error the pass carries on, loses the crop, and still writes an
    inventory — so a rate-limited cloud model produces a pass that exits cleanly,
    scores near zero, and is indistinguishable in the bake-off table from a model
    that simply reads badly. This exception is what lets the runner mark the pass
    INCOMPLETE instead of scoring it.

    ``retry_after`` is the server's own number in seconds when it sent one, and
    ``None`` when it did not — never a guess. It is the only evidence of how wide
    the limit window is, and inventing it would put a fabricated figure into the
    projection of what a full-volume sweep would cost.
    """

    def __init__(self, message: str, retry_after: float | None = None,
                 status: int | None = None):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.retry_after = retry_after
        self.status = status


#: What a spent quota says. Ollama Cloud fronts several providers and the wording
#: is theirs, not the daemon's, so this matches on the vocabulary they share
#: rather than on any one provider's sentence.
_RATE_LIMIT_WORDS = ("rate limit", "rate_limit", "ratelimit", "too many requests",
                     "quota", "insufficient_quota", "exceeded your current",
                     "usage limit", "capacity", "try again later")


def _rate_limit_from(status: int | None, text: str,
                     headers=None) -> RateLimited | None:
    """A :class:`RateLimited` if this reply is a spent quota, else ``None``.

    **Status first, then wording.** 429 is unambiguous and is taken on its own.
    Everything else has to name a limit, because Ollama Cloud returns a 200 with
    an ``error`` string for some upstream refusals and a bare 5xx for others — and
    a 5xx that says nothing about a quota is a broken request, which must stay an
    ordinary failure so it keeps being retried.
    """
    lowered = (text or "").lower()
    named = any(word in lowered for word in _RATE_LIMIT_WORDS)
    if status != 429 and not named:
        return None
    retry_after = None
    for header in ("retry-after", "x-ratelimit-reset-requests",
                   "x-ratelimit-reset-tokens"):
        raw = (headers or {}).get(header) if headers else None
        if raw:
            try:
                retry_after = float(str(raw).rstrip("s"))
                break
            except ValueError:
                continue
    return RateLimited((text or "rate limited")[:300], retry_after, status)


class ClaudeReader:
    """Channel A on the Claude API, via the official Anthropic SDK.

    The system prompt is cached, so on all but the first call it is a cache read at
    a tenth of the input rate — which is most of why a block costs under two cents.

    ``thinking`` is set **explicitly**. On Claude Opus 5 omitting it runs adaptive
    thinking (a change from Opus 4.8, where omitting it meant off), so leaving it
    to the default silently bought thinking tokens at the output rate on every
    block and made the cost estimate understate by a multiple. Disabling it is a
    real option here — this is transcription, not reasoning — but it carries the
    Opus 5 failure mode where internal tags leak into the visible response, which
    would fight the JSON schema, so ``effort`` is the lever to reach for first.
    """

    name = "claude"

    def __init__(self, model: str, effort: str, thinking: str = "adaptive",
                 max_tokens: int = 8000, system: str = TRANSCRIBE_SYSTEM,
                 schema: dict | None = None, payload_key: str = "rows"):
        import anthropic

        # gzip only: `anthropic` 1.x advertises brotli whenever a codec is
        # importable, and the brotlicffi on the machine of record fails while
        # decoding a reply the server has already acted on — see
        # ``lexikon_1910_pages.AnthropicPageReader.ACCEPT_ENCODING``.
        self.client = anthropic.Anthropic(
            default_headers={"Accept-Encoding": "gzip, deflate"})
        self.model = model
        self.effort = effort
        self.thinking = thinking
        self.max_tokens = max_tokens
        self.system = system
        self.schema = schema or ROW_SCHEMA
        self.payload_key = payload_key
        #: How many leading image parts every call of a pass repeats byte for
        #: byte — the symbol atlas. The cache breakpoint moves behind the last of
        #: them, so the atlas is read from the cache with the system prompt
        #: instead of being billed in full with every crop.
        self.shared_parts = 0

    def params(self, parts, instruction: str) -> dict:
        """The request for one call, apart from the client that sends it."""
        content: list[dict] = []
        for i, (image, caption) in enumerate(parts):
            content.append({"type": "image",
                            "source": {"type": "base64", "media_type": "image/png",
                                       "data": encode_png(image)}})
            if caption:
                content.append({"type": "text", "text": caption})
            if i + 1 == self.shared_parts:
                content[-1]["cache_control"] = {"type": "ephemeral"}
        content.append({"type": "text", "text": instruction})

        params = {
            "model": self.model,
            "max_tokens": self.max_tokens,
            "system": [{"type": "text", "text": self.system,
                        "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}],
            "output_config": {"format": {"type": "json_schema",
                                         "schema": self.schema}},
            "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}],
        }
        if self.thinking == "disabled":
            params["thinking"] = {"type": "disabled"}
        elif self.thinking == "adaptive":
            params["thinking"] = {"type": "adaptive"}
        if self.model not in NO_EFFORT:
            params["output_config"]["effort"] = self.effort
        return params

    def __call__(self, parts, instruction: str) -> tuple[list, dict]:
        response = self.client.messages.create(**self.params(parts, instruction))
        usage = {
            "input": response.usage.input_tokens,
            "output": response.usage.output_tokens,
            "cache_write": getattr(response.usage, "cache_creation_input_tokens", 0) or 0,
            "cache_read": getattr(response.usage, "cache_read_input_tokens", 0) or 0,
        }
        if response.stop_reason == "refusal":
            category = getattr(response.stop_details, "category", None)
            raise RuntimeError(f"refusal: {category}")
        # Reported before the JSON is touched: a truncated reply is unparseable
        # JSON, and without this it burns three retries and is filed as a generic
        # failure with the cause — the token cap — invisible.
        if response.stop_reason == "max_tokens":
            raise Truncated(f"hit max_tokens={self.max_tokens} "
                            f"({usage['output']} output tokens)")
        text = next((b.text for b in response.content if b.type == "text"), "")
        if not text:
            raise RuntimeError("no text block in reply "
                               f"(stop_reason={response.stop_reason})")
        return json.loads(text)[self.payload_key], usage


class OpenAICompatibleReader:
    """Any OpenAI-compatible vision endpoint, for either the table or the apparatus.

    Covers a hosted open-weights model and a local one with the same code, since
    vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio and most providers all expose ``/v1/chat/completions``
    with image content parts. Point ``--reader-url`` at the endpoint and
    ``--reader-model`` at the model id.

    The prompt and the schema are constructor arguments, so channel A (a block of
    the table, ``{"rows": [...]}``) and channel G (a crop of the footnote
    apparatus, ``{"lines": [...]}``) share one implementation. They also share the
    response-format degradation below, which is the part worth not writing twice:
    it is a small state machine about a provider's quirks, and a second copy of it
    would be a second thing to keep true.

    Two things differ from the Claude path and both are handled here rather than
    assumed. There is no prompt caching, so the system prompt is billed (or
    computed) in full on every call — irrelevant locally, not irrelevant on a
    hosted endpoint. And schema enforcement varies: ``json_schema`` is requested,
    then degraded to ``json_object``, then dropped altogether, and the reply is
    salvaged from a bare or fenced JSON object, because a model that cannot hold
    the schema should score as a worse reader rather than crash the run and score
    as nothing at all.

    The degradation is sticky: once an endpoint has rejected a response format,
    the working one is reused for every later block instead of paying a failed
    call per block to rediscover the same answer.
    """

    name = "openai-compatible"

    def __init__(self, model: str, base_url: str, api_key_env: str = "OPENAI_API_KEY",
                 system: str = TRANSCRIBE_SYSTEM, schema: dict | None = None,
                 payload_key: str = "rows", schema_name: str = "block",
                 max_tokens: int = 8000, text_lines: bool = False,
                 temperature: float | None = None,
                 reasoning_effort: str | None = None):
        from openai import OpenAI

        self.client = OpenAI(base_url=base_url,
                             api_key=os.environ.get(api_key_env, "not-needed"))
        self.model = model
        self.system = system
        self.schema = schema or ROW_SCHEMA
        self.payload_key = payload_key
        self.max_tokens = max_tokens
        #: Take the reply as printed lines rather than as JSON. A dedicated OCR
        #: model returns a page, not an object, and forcing a schema onto a
        #: half-billion-parameter decoder fails first on the hard pages.
        self.text_lines = text_lines
        #: Sampling temperature. **Transcription is not a creative task**, and the
        #: default is not neutral: Ollama samples at 0.8 unless told otherwise, and
        #: on ``glm-ocr`` that is the difference between a clean reading and a
        #: reply that wanders into LaTeX and then into commentary about which
        #: numbers looked bold. Two runs over the identical crop produced
        #: materially different output before this was set.
        self.temperature = temperature
        #: ``reasoning_effort`` as the endpoint takes it (``none`` switches Gemini's
        #: thinking off). None sends nothing, which on a thinking model means the
        #: provider's default — on Gemini 3.x Flash that is ~2,000–5,700 thinking
        #: tokens a crop, billed as output and invisible in ``completion_tokens``.
        self.reasoning_effort = reasoning_effort or None
        #: Tried in order, most enforced first. The text path asks for no format at
        #: all — there is nothing to degrade to, and requesting JSON from a model
        #: that will not produce it only spends a call to find that out.
        self.formats = [None] if text_lines else [
            {"type": "json_schema",
             "json_schema": {"name": schema_name, "schema": self.schema,
                             "strict": True}},
            {"type": "json_object"},
            None,
        ]
        self.format_index = 0

    def body(self, parts, instruction: str, format_index: int | None = None) -> dict:
        """The chat-completions request for one call, unsent — what a batch line carries."""
        kwargs = self._kwargs(self.format_index if format_index is None else format_index)
        content = []
        for image, caption in parts:
            content.append({"type": "image_url",
                            "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64,"
                                                 + encode_png(image)}})
            if caption:
                content.append({"type": "text", "text": caption})
        content.append({"type": "text", "text": instruction})
        return {"model": self.model, "max_tokens": self.max_tokens,
                "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": self.system},
                             {"role": "user", "content": content}], **kwargs}

    def _kwargs(self, format_index: int) -> dict:
        kwargs = {}
        if self.formats[format_index] is not None:
            kwargs["response_format"] = self.formats[format_index]
        if self.temperature is not None:
            kwargs["temperature"] = self.temperature
        if self.reasoning_effort:
            kwargs["reasoning_effort"] = self.reasoning_effort
        return kwargs

    def _create(self, parts, instruction: str, format_index: int):
        return self.client.chat.completions.create(**self.body(parts, instruction, format_index))

    def __call__(self, parts, instruction: str) -> tuple[list, dict]:
        response = None
        while response is None:
            try:
                response = self._create(parts, instruction, self.format_index)
            except Exception as exc:                        # noqa: BLE001
                # A SPENT QUOTA FIRST, because it is the one error that must not
                # be retried and the one the caller can act on. `_rate_limit_from`
                # was written for exactly this and was reachable only from
                # OllamaReader - so a 429 here raised the provider's own class,
                # missed `read_crop`'s `except RateLimited`, spent three more
                # requests against the exhausted quota, and wrote a pass that
                # scored near zero with NO ratelimit marker beside it saying why.
                # Indistinguishable, downstream, from a model that reads badly.
                limited = _rate_limit_from(
                    getattr(exc, "status_code", None), str(exc),
                    getattr(getattr(exc, "response", None), "headers", None))
                if limited is not None:
                    raise limited from exc
                # Only a rejected *response format* is worth degrading over. A
                # network fault must propagate to the caller's retry, or the run
                # would quietly drop to an unenforced schema because the endpoint
                # was briefly busy.
                if (self.format_index + 1 >= len(self.formats)
                        or not _is_format_rejection(exc)):
                    raise
                self.format_index += 1
                label = self.formats[self.format_index]
                print(f"  endpoint rejected the response format "
                      f"({type(exc).__name__}); falling back to "
                      f"{label['type'] if label else 'no response_format'}")
        # Ahead of the JSON, exactly as ClaudeReader checks its own stop_reason,
        # and for the reason that check documents: a truncated reply is
        # unparseable JSON, so without this it burns three retries and is filed
        # as a generic failure with the cause — the token cap — invisible.
        #
        # On a REASONING model that is the normal failure, not an edge case. The
        # thinking channel is billed and capped as output, so a budget that fits
        # an answer but not the deliberation before it returns empty content and
        # finish_reason="length". Downstream an empty region reads as a part of
        # the page that was blank, which is a lie about the source rather than a
        # gap in the run — and it is what a whole Gemini pass came back as on
        # 2026-08-29, 163 rows of text layer and not one from the image.
        #
        # `Truncated` is what makes the caller double max_tokens and retry, so
        # raising it here is also the precondition for measuring thinking at all
        # on a hosted reader: without it the experiment fails silently.
        if getattr(response.choices[0], "finish_reason", None) == "length":
            raise Truncated(
                f"hit max_tokens={self.max_tokens} (finish_reason=length, "
                f"{getattr(response.usage, 'completion_tokens', 0)} completion "
                f"tokens) — on a reasoning model the budget went to thinking")
        text = response.choices[0].message.content or ""
        # OUTPUT IS WHAT WAS BILLED AS OUTPUT, not what came back as text. On
        # Gemini's OpenAI-compatible endpoint `completion_tokens` is the answer
        # alone; the thinking the model does by default is billed at the output
        # rate and shows up only in `total_tokens`. Measured 2026-09-22 on one E1
        # crop: prompt 4,205, completion ~320, total ~9,600-10,200 on 3.8 — so the
        # E1 ledger's $0.32 a pass was really ~$1.95. `thinking` keeps the hidden
        # share visible rather than folding it in silently.
        prompt_tokens = getattr(response.usage, "prompt_tokens", 0) or 0
        completion_tokens = getattr(response.usage, "completion_tokens", 0) or 0
        total_tokens = getattr(response.usage, "total_tokens", 0) or 0
        hidden = max(total_tokens - prompt_tokens - completion_tokens, 0)
        usage = {
            "input": prompt_tokens,
            "output": completion_tokens + hidden,
            "thinking": hidden,
            "cache_write": 0, "cache_read": 0,
        }
        # AN EMPTY REPLY IS NOT A MALFORMED ONE, and until 2026-08-29 this path
        # could not tell the difference: `_salvage_json("")` raised "no JSON
        # object in reply", the caller filed a generic failure, and three
        # identical retries later a whole pass came back as channel B alone.
        #
        # The numbers separate the causes, so report them instead of the guess.
        # A reasoning model that spent the budget deliberating has a large
        # `completion_tokens` (and, where the endpoint reports it,
        # `reasoning_tokens`) against zero characters of content — that is the
        # budget, and raising max_tokens is the fix. Content empty with FEW
        # completion tokens is the opposite: the model returned early, and a
        # bigger budget would change nothing.
        if not text:
            details = getattr(response.usage, "completion_tokens_details", None)
            reasoning = getattr(details, "reasoning_tokens", None)
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"empty reply from {self.model}: "
                f"finish_reason={getattr(response.choices[0], 'finish_reason', None)!r}, "
                f"{usage['output']} completion tokens"
                + (f" of which {reasoning} reasoning" if reasoning is not None
                   else " (endpoint reports no reasoning split)")
                + f", max_tokens={self.max_tokens}")
        if self.text_lines:
            from utils.lexikon_1910 import lexikon_1910_vision as lxv

            return lxv.lines_from_text(text), usage
        return _salvage_json(text).get(self.payload_key, []), usage


class OllamaReader:
    """A local Ollama daemon on its **native** ``/api/chat`` endpoint.

    Not the OpenAI-compatible layer, for one decisive reason: **thinking cannot be
    turned off through it**. ``qwen3.5`` reasons by default, and on a transcription
    prompt it spent its entire token budget in the reasoning channel and returned
    an empty ``content`` with ``done_reason=length`` — a 56-second call that
    produced nothing, and which the OpenAI path reports as "no JSON object in
    reply" with no hint of the cause. The same model with ``think: false`` answers
    in 4.6 seconds and reads a legend entry the OCR model drops.

    Two further things the native API gives that the compatibility layer does not,
    both of which matter more here than portability:

    * ``format`` takes a **JSON schema object**, so structured output is enforced
      by the daemon's own grammar rather than requested politely and salvaged.
    * ``options.num_predict`` and ``options.temperature`` are explicit. The
      temperature default is 0.8, which on a small model is the difference between
      a transcription and a monologue.

    ``keep_alive`` holds the weights in VRAM between crops. Without it a run of a
    few hundred crops pays the model load repeatedly, and on a 12 GB card that
    load is most of the wall clock.
    """

    name = "ollama"

    def __init__(self, model: str, base_url: str = "http://127.0.0.1:11434",
                 system: str = TRANSCRIBE_SYSTEM, schema: dict | None = None,
                 payload_key: str = "rows", max_tokens: int = 4000,
                 text_lines: bool = False, temperature: float = 0.0,
                 think: bool = False, keep_alive: str = "10m",
                 num_ctx: int = 0):
        self.url = base_url.rstrip("/").removesuffix("/v1") + "/api/chat"
        self.model = model
        self.system = system
        self.schema = schema
        self.payload_key = payload_key
        self.max_tokens = max_tokens
        self.text_lines = text_lines
        self.temperature = temperature
        self.think = think
        self.keep_alive = keep_alive
        #: Ollama defaults this to 4096 whatever the model can hold, and the
        #: default silently *slides the window* rather than erroring — so a prompt
        #: that grows past it loses its head, which here is the system prompt and
        #: the reference image. Sending a symbol atlas alongside the crop roughly
        #: doubles the input, so it has to be set explicitly or the atlas pushes
        #: the instructions out of context and nothing says so.
        self.num_ctx = num_ctx

    def __call__(self, parts, instruction: str) -> tuple[list, dict]:
        import requests

        images = [encode_png(image) for image, _caption in parts]
        captions = " ".join(c for _i, c in parts if c)
        body = {
            "model": self.model,
            "stream": False,
            "think": self.think,
            "keep_alive": self.keep_alive,
            "options": {"temperature": self.temperature,
                        "num_predict": self.max_tokens,
                        **({"num_ctx": self.num_ctx} if self.num_ctx else {})},
            "messages": [
                {"role": "system", "content": self.system},
                {"role": "user",
                 "content": f"{captions}\n{instruction}".strip(),
                 "images": images},
            ],
        }
        if self.schema is not None and not self.text_lines:
            body["format"] = self.schema
        response = requests.post(self.url, json=body, timeout=900)
        # A CLOUD MODEL REFUSES IN TWO SHAPES AND BOTH ARRIVE HERE. `glm-5.3-flash:cloud`
        # and its siblings are served through this same local daemon, which
        # forwards the provider's answer: a spent quota comes back either as a
        # 429, or as a 200 carrying an `error` string. Checking only the status
        # would let the second shape through as an ordinary failure — retried
        # three times, counted as a bad read, and then averaged into the model's
        # score as if it had looked at the page.
        #
        # **THE BODY IS ONLY EVER INSPECTED ON A FAILURE.** The first version of
        # this ran the wording test over `response.text` of every reply, 200s
        # included — so a model that happened to transcribe the word "capacity"
        # or "quota" would have been read as rate limited, parking it and
        # silently abandoning the rest of the pass. A successful reply is trusted
        # to be a reading; only an explicit error is searched for a limit.
        if response.status_code >= 400:
            limited = _rate_limit_from(response.status_code, response.text,
                                       response.headers)
            if limited is not None:
                raise limited
        response.raise_for_status()
        data = response.json()
        if "error" in data:
            limited = _rate_limit_from(None, str(data["error"]),
                                       response.headers)
            if limited is not None:
                raise limited
            raise RuntimeError(str(data["error"])[:300])
        message = data.get("message", {})
        usage = {"input": data.get("prompt_eval_count", 0) or 0,
                 "output": data.get("eval_count", 0) or 0,
                 "cache_write": 0, "cache_read": 0}
        text = message.get("content") or ""
        if not text:
            # Distinguish the two ways a local model returns nothing, because the
            # fixes are opposite: a budget spent on reasoning needs thinking off,
            # a budget spent on output needs a bigger one.
            thinking = message.get("thinking") or ""
            if thinking:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    f"empty reply: the model spent {usage['output']} tokens "
                    f"thinking ({len(thinking)} chars) and emitted no content. "
                    f"Run with --notes-think off (the default)")
            if data.get("done_reason") == "length":
                raise Truncated(f"hit num_predict={self.max_tokens}")
            raise RuntimeError(f"empty reply (done_reason="
                               f"{data.get('done_reason')})")
        if self.text_lines:
            from utils.lexikon_1910 import lexikon_1910_vision as lxv

            return lxv.lines_from_text(text), usage
        return _salvage_json(text).get(self.payload_key, []), usage


def _is_format_rejection(exc: Exception) -> bool:
    """Is this the endpoint refusing the response format, or a real fault?"""
    status = getattr(exc, "status_code", None)
    if status is not None and status not in (400, 404, 422):
        return False
    message = str(exc).lower()
    return any(token in message for token in
               ("response_format", "json_schema", "schema", "strict",
                "not supported", "unsupported", "unknown parameter",
                "invalid parameter"))


def _salvage_json(text: str) -> dict:
    """Parse a model reply that may or may not have honoured the schema."""
    text = text.strip()
    if text.startswith("```"):
        text = re.sub(r"^```(?:json)?\s*|\s*```$", "", text, flags=re.MULTILINE)
    try:
        return json.loads(text)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        pass
    start, end = text.find("{"), text.rfind("}")
    if start != -1 and end > start:
        return json.loads(text[start:end + 1])
    raise ValueError(f"no JSON object in reply: {text[:120]!r}")


def build_reader(args):
    """Pick the channel-A reader.

    The reader is the only model-specific part of the pipeline. The grid, the block
    segmentation, the invariants, the anchoring and the grader are all downstream of
    it and none of them know which model produced the rows — so a candidate reader
    can be scored against exactly the same yardstick, and a cheap reader can be run
    on every block with an expensive one reserved for the blocks it fails.
    """
    if args.reader == "claude":
        return ClaudeReader(args.model, args.effort, thinking=args.thinking,
                            max_tokens=args.max_tokens)
    base_url, key_env = READER_ENDPOINTS.get(
        args.reader, (args.reader_url, "OPENAI_API_KEY"))
    if args.reader in READER_ENDPOINTS and not args.reader_model:
        raise SystemExit(
            f"--reader {args.reader} needs --reader-model: the vision model ids at "
            f"{base_url} change often enough that this script does not guess one. "
            f"Take the id from the provider's current model list.")
    # TEMPERATURE IS PASSED, and before this it was not. `OpenAICompatibleReader`
    # takes one and sends it only when it is not None; `build_reader` never
    # supplied it, so every channel-A pass through a local daemon ran at Ollama's
    # default 0.8 — which the reader's own docstring records as the difference
    # between a clean reading and a reply that wanders into LaTeX. Channel G was
    # never exposed to this because `build_notes_reader` has always passed
    # `--notes-temperature`.
    return OpenAICompatibleReader(args.reader_model or args.model,
                                  base_url, args.reader_key_env or key_env,
                                  temperature=args.reader_temperature,
                                  reasoning_effort=args.reader_reasoning_effort or None)


def block_parts(tiles) -> tuple[list[tuple], str]:
    """Channel A's images and their captions, from :func:`lx.tile_block` output."""
    parts = []
    for image, first, last in tiles:
        caption = ""
        if len(tiles) > 1:
            names = ", ".join(f"{i + 1} {lx.COL_NAMES[i]}"
                              for i in range(first, last + 1))
            caption = (f"The image above shows columns 1 seq and 2 name (repeated "
                       f"on every image so the rows line up), then columns {names}.")
        parts.append((image, caption))
    instruction = ("Transcribe this block. Every image shows the same rows."
                   if len(tiles) > 1 else "Transcribe this block.")
    return parts, instruction


def build_notes_reader(args, abbreviations, section: str = "", quiet: bool = False):
    """The channel-G reader — the apparatus below the table, read from the image.

    Separate from :func:`build_reader` on purpose. The two channels are different
    jobs on different type at different prices, and the whole point of the split is
    that the expensive reader can be off while this one runs: the apparatus is
    where the text layer fails outright, and it is three crops a page rather than
    fifteen blocks.

    ``--notes-reader claude`` exists so the same crops can be scored against a
    reference reader on a handful of pages, not because it is the intended
    production path.

    The prompt style and the reply format both default to *what the named model is
    built for*, and both can be overridden. A dedicated OCR model gets the
    transcription prompt and a plain-text reply; a general vision-language model
    gets the closed symbol list and a JSON schema. Guessing this from the model id
    is a heuristic, so it is announced in the run and never silent.

    ``section`` says the crops are single sections rather than whole columns, and
    is passed straight to the prompt builder: one kind of entry described instead
    of five, and only the symbols that kind of section prints. One reader is built
    per section kind, which is why this can be called more than once and why
    ``quiet`` exists.
    """
    from utils.lexikon_1910 import lexikon_1910_vision as lxv

    model_id = args.notes_model or args.model
    ocr_shaped = any(mark in model_id.lower() for mark in OCR_MODEL_MARKS)
    style = args.notes_style or ("transcribe" if ocr_shaped else "annotate")
    text_lines = (args.notes_format == "text"
                  or (args.notes_format == "auto" and ocr_shaped))
    system = lxv.build_system(abbreviations, style=style, section=section,
                              atlas=bool(getattr(args, "notes_atlas", False)),
                              think=bool(getattr(args, "notes_think", False)),
                              contrast=bool(getattr(args, "notes_contrast", "")))
    if not quiet:
        print(f"  prompt style: {style}; reply as "
              f"{'printed lines' if text_lines else 'JSON'}"
              + (f"; scoped to the {section} section "
                 f"({len(lxv.pictograms(abbreviations, section))} symbols, not "
                 f"{len(lxv.pictograms(abbreviations))})" if section else "")
              + ("  (from the model id — override with --notes-style/"
                 "--notes-format)"
                 if not (args.notes_style and args.notes_format != "auto")
                 else ""))

    def tagged(reader):
        # What was actually sent, recorded on the object that sent it. The join
        # needs to know whether this pass was asked to *name* symbols or only to
        # mark where they were, and re-deriving that from the model id at the call
        # site would drift the moment --notes-style overrides the guess.
        reader.prompt_style = style
        return reader

    if args.notes_reader == "claude":
        return tagged(ClaudeReader(args.model, args.effort, thinking=args.thinking,
                                   max_tokens=args.max_tokens, system=system,
                                   schema=lxv.NOTES_SCHEMA, payload_key="lines"))
    base_url, key_env = READER_ENDPOINTS.get(
        args.notes_reader, (args.reader_url, "OPENAI_API_KEY"))
    if args.notes_reader == "ollama":
        if not args.notes_model:
            raise SystemExit("--notes-reader ollama needs --notes-model; "
                             "run --list-models to see what is pulled")
        return tagged(OllamaReader(args.notes_model, base_url, system=system,
                                   schema=lxv.NOTES_SCHEMA, payload_key="lines",
                                   max_tokens=args.notes_max_tokens,
                                   text_lines=text_lines,
                                   temperature=args.notes_temperature,
                                   think=args.notes_think,
                                   num_ctx=args.notes_num_ctx))
    if not args.notes_model:
        raise SystemExit(
            f"--channels G needs --notes-model: the vision model ids at {base_url} "
            f"change often enough that this script does not guess one. Take the id "
            f"from the provider's current model list.")
    return tagged(OpenAICompatibleReader(
        args.notes_model, base_url, args.notes_key_env or key_env,
        system=system, schema=lxv.NOTES_SCHEMA, payload_key="lines",
        schema_name="notes", max_tokens=args.notes_max_tokens,
        text_lines=text_lines, temperature=args.notes_temperature,
        reasoning_effort=getattr(args, "notes_reasoning_effort", "") or None))


def parse_price(spec: str) -> tuple[float, float] | None:
    """``"0.6,1.8"`` -> USD per million input / output tokens."""
    if not spec:
        return None
    try:
        rate_in, rate_out = (float(p) for p in spec.split(","))
    except ValueError:
        raise SystemExit("--reader-price wants IN,OUT in USD per million tokens, "
                         f"e.g. 0.6,1.8 — got {spec!r}")
    return rate_in, rate_out


def table_rows(blocks_by_page: dict, a_raw: dict) -> list[dict]:
    """Every table row each channel read, one per printed line, for the scorer.

    Channel B's rows are the text layer's on each block, in printed order with
    the *mezi tím* lines in place; channel A's are the model's reply on the same
    block, kept whole. Both are keyed by the block, so a gold row can be matched
    to the same crop in either channel (``score_table_passes.py``).
    """
    out = []
    for stem, blocks in blocks_by_page.items():
        for block in blocks:
            base = {"page": stem, "block_id": block.block_id,
                    "block_index": block.index, "okres_label": block.okres_label,
                    "court_label": block.court_label}
            printed = sorted(block.rows + block.of_which, key=lambda r: r.top)
            for n, row in enumerate(printed):
                out.append({"channel": "B", **base, "row": n,
                            **{c: row.get(c) for c in lx.COL_NAMES}})
            for n, row in enumerate(a_raw.get(block.block_id, [])):
                out.append({"channel": "A", **base, "row": n,
                            **{c: (row.get(c) or "").strip() for c in lx.COL_NAMES}})
    return out


def rows_to_block(page_stem: str, index: int, rows: list[dict]) -> lx.Block | None:
    """Rebuild a :class:`~utils.lexikon_1910.lexikon_1910.Block` from the model's rows.

    Segmentation uses the same rule as channel B — the area column marks the
    municipality line — so the two channels are compared on the same object rather
    than on whatever each one decided a block was.
    """
    parsed = [lx.Row(page=page_stem, top=0, bottom=0,
                     cells={c: (r.get(c) or "").strip() for c in lx.COL_NAMES})
              for r in rows]
    blocks, _orphans = lx.segment_blocks(parsed)
    if not blocks:
        return None
    block = blocks[0]
    block.index = index
    return block


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Cross-channel agreement
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

def compare_channels(left, right, label: str) -> list[dict]:
    """Cell-by-cell agreement between two channels on one block.

    Compares the municipality row and, where both channels found the same number of
    settlements, the settlement rows too. Where the row counts differ the block is
    reported as a structural disagreement rather than aligned by position — an
    off-by-one alignment would score every later row as a mismatch and bury the one
    real finding.
    """
    findings: list[dict] = []
    pairs = [(left.municipality, right.municipality, "municipality")]
    if len(left.settlements) == len(right.settlements):
        pairs += [(a, b, "settlement")
                  for a, b in zip(left.settlements, right.settlements)]
    else:
        findings.append({
            "block_id": left.block_id, "row_kind": "block",
            "row_name": left.name, "check": f"{label}:row_count",
            "verdict": "fail",
            "detail": f"{len(left.settlements)} vs {len(right.settlements)} settlements",
        })

    for a, b, kind in pairs:
        for column in lx.INT_COLS:
            a_value, a_status = lx.parse_int_cell(a.get(column))
            b_value, b_status = lx.parse_int_cell(b.get(column))
            if a_status == "bad" or b_status == "bad":
                verdict = "unparseable"
            elif a_status == "blank" and b_status == "blank":
                verdict = "na"
            elif (a_value or 0) == (b_value or 0):
                verdict = "pass"
            else:
                verdict = "fail"
            findings.append({
                "block_id": left.block_id, "row_kind": kind,
                "row_name": a.get("name"), "check": f"{label}:{column}",
                "verdict": verdict,
                "detail": "" if verdict in ("pass", "na")
                          else f"{a.get(column)!r} vs {b.get(column)!r}",
            })
    return findings


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Runner
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

def parse_pages(spec: str) -> list[int]:
    pages: list[int] = []
    for part in spec.split(","):
        if "-" in part:
            start, end = part.split("-")
            pages += list(range(int(start), int(end) + 1))
        else:
            pages.append(int(part))
    return pages


def write_json(path: Path, payload: dict) -> None:
    """Write one small JSON record — a marker, not a dataset."""
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False),
                    encoding="utf-8")


def write_csv(path: Path, records: list[dict]) -> None:
    """Write records to CSV, keyed on the union of their fields.

    Taking the header from ``records[0]`` alone would raise the moment a check
    emits a verdict that carries an extra field — an ``unmatched`` finding has no
    ``column``, for instance — and would do it at write time, after the whole run.
    First-seen order is preserved so the columns stay readable.
    """
    if not records:
        return
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fields: list[str] = []
    for record in records:
        fields += [k for k in record if k not in fields]
    with path.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=fields, restval="")
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(records)


def probe_reader(args, abbreviations, page_number: int = 118) -> int:
    """Send one real crop to the reader and report what came back, and how fast.

    The question a local reader has to answer first is not "how accurate" but
    **"can it see at all"**. A text-only model at a vision endpoint does not fail
    loudly: many silently ignore the image and answer from the prompt, which
    produces plausible, entirely invented lines — the single worst failure mode
    available here, because every downstream check would be grading fiction.

    So the probe sends the *footer* crop of a real page, which is the smallest one
    and carries the postal legend: a short list of Czech place names. If the reply
    contains place names that are printed on that page, the model saw the image. If
    it contains fluent Czech that is not on the page, it did not — and that is
    visible to a human in ten seconds, which is the point of printing the reply
    rather than scoring it.

    The elapsed time is the other half. On a local daemon the volume's feasibility
    is a wall-clock question, and one crop answers it to within a factor that
    matters: at 20 s a crop the apparatus is an overnight job, at 120 s it is a
    fortnight.
    """
    from utils.lexikon_1910 import lexikon_1910_vision as lxv

    page = lx.read_alto(CZ_PAGES / f"{page_number:04d}.alto.xml")
    notes = lxnt.extract_notes(page)
    if notes is None:
        print(f"  page {page_number} has no footnote divider — pick another")
        return 1
    image = lx.render_page(CZ_PDF, page_number, page.width)
    section = ""
    reference_lines = notes.footer_lines
    if args.notes_sections:
        # Probe the crop the run will actually send. The footer is the smallest
        # region on the page and the easiest thing on it to read; measuring a
        # section pass on the footer would answer a question nobody asked.
        kinds = (("parts", "offices") if args.notes_sections == "all"
                 else (args.notes_sections,))
        wanted = [s for s in lxnt.section_segments(notes, page)
                  if s.kind in kinds]
        if not wanted:
            print(f"  page {page_number} has no {args.notes_sections} section — "
                  f"pick another with --probe-page")
            return 1
        # The tallest one: the probe should measure the hard case, because that is
        # where a small reader truncates and where the wall clock is decided.
        target = max(wanted, key=lambda s: s.height)
        crops = [(c, f"{s.kind}/{s.district}") for c, s, _i, _n in
                 lxnt.crop_segments(image, [target], page,
                                    target_width=args.notes_width or None,
                                    upscale=args.notes_upscale,
                                    slices=args.notes_slices,
                                    max_height=args.notes_max_height)]
        section = target.kind
        reference_lines = target.lines
        print(f"  page {page_number} has {len(wanted)} {args.notes_sections} "
              f"section(s); probing the tallest ({target.district}, "
              f"{target.height} px, {len(target.lines)} lines)")
    else:
        crops = [(c, r) for c, r in
                 lxnt.crop_notes(image, notes, page, regions=("footer",),
                                 target_width=args.notes_width or None,
                                 upscale=args.notes_upscale,
                                 slices=args.notes_slices,
                                 max_height=args.notes_max_height)]
    if not crops:
        print(f"  page {page_number} has nothing to crop — pick another")
        return 1
    crop, region = crops[0]
    print(f"  probe: page {page_number}, {region} crop, "
          f"{crop.width}x{crop.height} px"
          + (f"  (1 of {len(crops)} strips)" if len(crops) > 1 else ""))

    reader = build_notes_reader(args, abbreviations, section=section)
    started = time.time()
    try:
        lines, usage = reader([(crop, f"This image is one section of the footnote "
                                      f"apparatus." if section else
                                f"This image is the {region} region of the "
                                f"footnote apparatus.")],
                              "Transcribe this image.")
    except Exception as exc:                            # noqa: BLE001
        print(f"  FAILED after {time.time() - started:.1f}s — "
              f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
        print("  a 400 mentioning images usually means the model is text-only; "
              "check the tag has a vision variant")
        return 1
    elapsed = time.time() - started

    deduped, repeats = lxv.drop_repeats([str(line) for line in lines])
    clean, rejected = lxv.guard_tokens(deduped, lxv.vocabulary(abbreviations))
    print(f"  {len(lines)} lines in {elapsed:.1f}s"
          + (f" ({usage.get('input', 0):,} in / {usage.get('output', 0):,} out "
             f"tokens)" if usage.get("input") else ""))
    if repeats:
        print(f"  ! {repeats} of them repeated an earlier line — the reader "
              f"looped; dropped, and reported because every consumer sums")
    if rejected:
        print(f"  tokens off the closed list: {dict(rejected)}")
    symbols = sum(line.count("[") for line in clean)
    print(f"  symbol tokens in the reply: {symbols}"
          + ("  — this reader transcribes the words and omits the pictograms, so "
             "it cannot build the institution inventory" if symbols == 0 else ""))
    print()
    for line in clean[:12]:
        print(f"    | {line[:110]}")
    if len(clean) > 12:
        print(f"    | ... {len(clean) - 12} more")
    if section == "offices" and reference_lines:
        # The decisive question, and only a targeted crop can ask it: does the
        # reply name the municipalities this section actually holds? Those numbers
        # cannot be guessed from a description of the format, so a reply that
        # misses them entirely was written from the prompt and not from the image.
        probe_section = lxv.sections_from_segments([(target, clean)])
        alto_section = lxv.sections_from_segments([(target, target.lines)])
        for finding in lxv.content_check(alto_section, probe_section):
            if finding["verdict"] == "invented":
                print()
                print(f"  !! {finding['detail']}")
                print(f"     This is the failure that does not look like one: a "
                      f"text-only model at a")
                print(f"     vision endpoint answers fluently from the prompt. "
                      f"Check the tag has a")
                print(f"     vision variant before spending a run on it.")
            elif finding["verdict"] == "pass":
                print(f"  content: {finding['detail']} — the reader saw the image")

    print()
    print("  compare against the text layer's reading of the same print:")
    for line in reference_lines[:8]:
        print(f"    B | {line[:110]}")
    # Only when the crop *is* the whole section. With more than one strip the
    # reference covers print this call was never shown, and comparing against it
    # would report every multi-strip probe as a truncation.
    if (len(crops) == 1 and reference_lines
            and len(clean) < len(reference_lines) * 0.6):
        print()
        print(f"  ! the image read returned {len(clean)} lines where the text "
              f"layer found {len(reference_lines)} on the same print.")
        print(f"    That is the truncation signature: the reader stops partway "
              f"down a crop it cannot")
        print(f"    hold. Cut it smaller with --notes-max-height (try "
              f"{max(200, crop.height // 2)}) and probe again.")
    print()
