    # Reported as a range because one measurement is one measurement: the first
    # call includes model load, and a warm daemon is faster.
    volume_blocks = VOLUME_BLOCKS
    # Sections are not three a page. Over the volume the register cuts ~2,155
    # offices sections and ~2,140 parts sections — measured, not assumed — so a
    # targeted pass is priced on its own crop count, not the region form's.
    per_page = (VOLUME_SECTIONS_PER_PAGE.get(args.notes_sections, 3.0)
                if args.notes_sections else 3.0)
    per_volume = N_TABLE_PAGES * per_page * elapsed / 3600
    table = volume_blocks * elapsed / 3600
    print(f"  at {elapsed:.1f}s/crop the whole Čechy apparatus "
          f"({round(N_TABLE_PAGES * per_page):,} crops) is "
          f"~{per_volume:.0f} h of wall clock on this machine, serial")
    print(f"  the table as well (~{volume_blocks:,} blocks) would be ~{table:.0f} h more"
          + ("  — at this rate a free second reading of the table is an "
             "overnight job, so channel A is worth running with this reader "
             "(--channels A --reader ollama)" if table < 24 else
             "  — which is why channel A is off by default"))
    if elapsed > 8:
        print("  ! that is slow for a crop this size. Check --notes-temperature 0 "
              "(a sampling default makes a small model wander) and that the model "
              "is warm — the first call includes the load")
    return 0


#: Everything :func:`apparatus_pass` can run. A targeted pass reads only some of
#: the apparatus, so it must be able to ask for only the consumers that reading
#: can feed — running the postal legend over crops that never contained it would
#: report every reference as "no legend" and bury the real result.
APPARATUS_CONSUMERS = ("parts", "places", "institutions")


def heading_reader(args, abbreviations, out_dir: Path):
    """``read(crop) -> str``: one section heading read off the image.

    Used only for a heading the image finds and the text layer lost entirely
    (``lexikon_1910_notes.image_section_segments``) — seven on the Czech table
    scans, 41 by the image's count. The general apparatus prompt reads it; the
    first line of the reply is the heading's text, and the section's kind and
    district are taken from it by ``find_heading``, never assumed. Cached per
    pass label on the crop's bytes, the model and the prompt, as the crops are.
    """
    reader = build_notes_reader(args, abbreviations, quiet=True)
    cache = out_dir / "crop_cache" / (args.notes_label or "unlabelled") / "headings"
    cache.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    def read(crop) -> str:
        key = hashlib.sha256(encode_png(crop).encode("utf-8")
                             + str(getattr(reader, "model", "")).encode("utf-8")
                             + str(getattr(reader, "system", "")).encode("utf-8")
                             ).hexdigest()
        hit = cache / f"{key}.json"
        if hit.exists():
            return json.loads(hit.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["text"]
        try:
            lines, _usage = reader([(crop, "This image is one line of the footnote "
                                           "apparatus, a section heading.")],
                                   "Transcribe this image.")
        except Exception as exc:                        # noqa: BLE001
            print(f"    heading read failed: {exc}")
            return ""
        text = " ".join(str(line) for line in (lines or []))
        hit.write_text(json.dumps({"text": text}), encoding="utf-8")
        return text

    return read


#: The register's line pitch in the apparatus, Czech-render pixels (two lines of
#: six-point type, top to top, ~36-40 px on scans 0076 0196 0316 0436).
LINE_PITCH = 38

#: A crop whose reply holds fewer than this share of its printed lines, or more
#: than the inverse, is flagged. A flag routes the crop to a look; it never
#: changes what was read (D-38).
LINE_SHARE_FLAG = 0.6


def printed_line_count(ink, box, page_width: int) -> int:
    """How many printed lines the image shows in ``box``.

    ``lexikon_1910_image.lines_in`` finds bands of ink; a band taller than one
    line (lines whose descenders and accents touch) counts as its height over the
    line pitch, so a dense block is not counted as one line.
    """
    from utils.lexikon_1910 import lexikon_1910_image as lximg

    scale = page_width / lximg.REFERENCE_WIDTH
    pitch = LINE_PITCH * scale
    return sum(max(1, round(line.height / pitch))
               for line in lximg.lines_in(ink, box, scale))


def crop_audit(lines_by_slot: dict, segment_by_slot: dict,
               printed_lines: dict) -> list[dict]:
    """One row per section read: what the image shows against what came back.

    * ``printed`` and ``returned`` lines, and a ``line_flag`` when the reply
      holds under 60 % or over 1/0.6 of them — a reader that skipped lines, or
      one that split them, looks different here from one that read them;
    * any section heading the reader wrote out (``find_heading`` on its lines)
      and whether its kind and district agree with the label the crop was cut
      under (``heading_flag``). The reader is never told the label, so a heading
      it transcribes is an independent reading of it.

    A record of the pass, never a repair: nothing read is changed here (D-38).
    """
    rows = []
    for slot, segment in sorted(segment_by_slot.items(),
                                key=lambda kv: (kv[0][0], kv[0][2])):
        lines = lines_by_slot.get(slot, [])
        printed = printed_lines.get(slot)
        seen = [h for h in (lxnt.find_heading(str(line)) for line in lines) if h]
        agree = [h for h in seen if h[0] == segment.kind
                 and lxnt.normalise(h[1]) == lxnt.normalise(segment.district)]
        share = (len(lines) / printed) if printed else None
        rows.append({
            "page": slot[0], "region": slot[1], "order": slot[2],
            "kind": segment.kind, "district": segment.district,
            "carried": int(segment.carried),
            "printed_lines": "" if printed is None else printed,
            "returned_lines": len(lines),
            "line_flag": int(share is not None and (share < LINE_SHARE_FLAG
                                                    or share > 1 / LINE_SHARE_FLAG)),
            "headings_in_reply": " | ".join(f"{k}:{d}" for k, d, _e in seen),
            "heading_flag": int(segment.kind in ("parts", "offices")
                                and bool(seen) and not agree),
        })
    flagged = [r for r in rows if r["line_flag"] or r["heading_flag"]]
    print(f"  crop audit: {len(rows)} sections; {sum(r['line_flag'] for r in rows)} "
          f"with a line count off by more than 40 %, "
          f"{sum(r['heading_flag'] for r in rows)} whose reply names a different "
          f"heading than the crop's label")
    for r in flagged[:8]:
        print(f"    {r['page']} {r['region']} {r['kind']}:{r['district'][:16]} "
              f"printed {r['printed_lines']} returned {r['returned_lines']} "
              f"{r['headings_in_reply'][:50]}")
    return rows


def image_cut_report(cuts) -> str:
    """What the image geometry did over a run's pages."""
    image = [c for c in cuts if c.geometry == "image"]
    unread = [(c.page, *h) for c in image for h in c.headings_image_unread]
    lines = [f"  geometry: image on {len(image)} of {len(cuts)} pages "
             f"({len(cuts) - len(image)} fell back to the text layer: no divider "
             f"in the image)",
             f"    headings: {sum(c.headings_both for c in image)} found by both, "
             f"{sum(c.headings_text_only for c in image)} by the text layer only, "
             f"{sum(c.headings_image_read for c in image)} by the image only and "
             f"labelled by a read of the line, {len(unread)} by the image only "
             f"and NOT labelled"]
    for page, region, top, text in unread[:10]:
        lines.append(f"      {page} {region} y={top}: {text[:60]!r} — the section "
                     f"runs on under the label before it")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def legend_pass(legend_lines: dict, notes_list, all_blocks, blocks_by_court,
                abbreviations, out_dir: Path, prefix: str, suffix: str) -> list[dict]:
    """The postal legend as the image read it, resolved and set against the text layer's."""
    pages = sorted(legend_lines)
    vision = [lxnt.Notes(page=page, top=0, bottom=0, split_x=0,
                         footer_lines=list(legend_lines[page])) for page in pages]
    records = apparatus_pass(vision, all_blocks, blocks_by_court, abbreviations,
                             out_dir, prefix=prefix, suffix=suffix, sections=[],
                             consumers=("places",))
    read = lxnt.postal_legend(vision)
    text = lxnt.postal_legend([n for n in notes_list if n.page in set(pages)])
    both = [(d, k) for d in read for k in read[d] if k in text.get(d, {})]
    same = sum(1 for d, k in both
               if lxnt.normalise(read[d][k].place) == lxnt.normalise(text[d][k].place))
    print(f"  legend: {sum(len(v) for v in read.values())} keys read from the image, "
          f"{sum(len(v) for v in text.values())} in the text layer; on the "
          f"{len(both)} both have, the place agrees on {same}")
    return records


def apparatus_pass(notes_list, all_blocks, blocks_by_court, abbreviations,
                   out_dir: Path, prefix: str = "", suffix: str = "",
                   sections=None, consumers=APPARATUS_CONSUMERS) -> list[dict]:
    """Everything the footnote apparatus yields, for *one* reading of it.

    Called once per channel — the ALTO text layer and, when channel G runs, the
    image read — with the same consumers in the same order. Factored out precisely
    so it cannot drift: two readings graded by two copies of this wiring would
    differ partly because the readings differ and partly because the wiring did,
    and there would be no way to tell the two apart afterwards.

    ``prefix`` tags the channel (``""`` for the text layer, ``"G:"`` for the image
    read) and ``suffix`` keeps the two sets of CSVs side by side rather than one
    overwriting the other.

    ``sections`` overrides the cut. A section-targeted pass has no ``Notes`` of its
    own — its crops were cut on the headings, not on the columns — so it hands the
    sections in directly and the same consumers run on them unchanged.
    """
    records: list[dict] = []
    if sections is None:
        sections = lxnt.collect_sections(notes_list)

    if "parts" in consumers:
        parts_findings = lxnt.parts_check(all_blocks, sections)
        for finding in parts_findings:
            finding["channel"] = f"{prefix}notes"
        records += parts_findings
        write_csv(out_dir / f"footnote_parts{suffix}.csv", parts_findings)
        # The named parts THEMSELVES, in the frame the gold sheets are read into
        # (D-49). The findings above grade a part's figures against the table;
        # this is what lets its place-type symbol be scored at all. Until
        # 2026-10-06 the parts were read, checked and then not written anywhere.
        write_csv(out_dir / f"parts{suffix}.csv",
                  lxnt.parts_records(sections, source=prefix.rstrip(":") or "text"))
        if notes_list:
            print(lxnt.lexikon_1910_notes_report(notes_list, sections,
                                                 parts_findings))

    if "places" in consumers:
        legend = lxnt.postal_legend(notes_list)
        place_records = lxnt.resolve_places(blocks_by_court, legend)
        for record in place_records:
            record["channel"] = f"{prefix}places"
        records += place_records
        write_csv(out_dir / f"place_keys{suffix}.csv", place_records)
        write_csv(out_dir / f"postal_legend{suffix}.csv",
                  [{"district": d, "key": k, "place": e.place,
                    "rail_symbol": e.rail_symbol, "page": e.page,
                    "key_printed": e.key_printed}
                   for d, entries in sorted(legend.items())
                   for k, e in sorted(entries.items())])
        print(lxnt.lexikon_1910_places_report(legend, place_records))

    if "institutions" in consumers and abbreviations:
        inst_records, inst_entries = lxin.decode_sections(sections, abbreviations)
        for record in inst_records:
            record["channel"] = f"{prefix}institutions"
        records += inst_records
        write_csv(out_dir / f"institutions{suffix}.csv", inst_records)
        # What is printed BESIDE the school and cooperative glyphs — classes and
        # language, kind and language — read off the same entries by the parser
        # the gold sheets go through. Its own file, never joined into `records`:
        # these are attributes of an institution, not further checks on a page.
        write_csv(out_dir / f"attributes{suffix}.csv",
                  lxat.attribute_records(lxat.entry_parts(inst_entries),
                                         source=prefix.rstrip(":") or "text"))
        print(lxin.lexikon_1910_institutions_report(
            inst_records, inst_entries, abbreviations))
    return records


def main() -> int:
    # THE REPORTS ARE NOT ASCII AND THE WINDOWS CONSOLE IS NOT UTF-8. The parts
    # ledger prints the marks the OCR engine actually returned — `Ш`, `©`, `«“■`
    # — and a Czech Windows console encodes cp1250, where the first of those has
    # no code point at all. `print` then raises UnicodeEncodeError *in the middle
    # of a finished pass*: the crops have been read and paid for, and the run
    # dies before it writes the inventory. Driven from `bakeoff.run_pilot` it is
    # worse than a crash, because the exception is caught, the pass is recorded
    # as a failure, and three of them in a row abort the rest of the matrix — a
    # night ended by a character the terminal could not draw.
    #
    # `errors="replace"` and not "strict": a mark that cannot be shown is a
    # question mark on the screen, never a lost pass.
    for stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
        try:
            stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        except (AttributeError, ValueError):
            pass
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--pages", default="118-137",
                    help="Čechy page numbers, e.g. 118-137 or 118,120,131")
    ap.add_argument("--channels", default="B,G,C",
                    help="which channels to run: B=ALTO text layer, G=apparatus "
                         "read from the image, C=German volume, A=the table read "
                         "by a vision model. A is off by default — it is the only "
                         "channel that bills per municipality")
    ap.add_argument("--model", default="claude-opus-5", choices=sorted(PRICING))
    ap.add_argument("--reader", default="claude",
                    choices=["claude", "openai-compatible", *READER_ENDPOINTS],
                    help="which model reads the block crops in channel A "
                         "(glm/glm-cn preset the Z.ai and Zhipu endpoints)")
    ap.add_argument("--reader-url", default="http://localhost:8000/v1",
                    help="base URL for an OpenAI-compatible vision endpoint "
                         "(vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio, or a hosted provider); "
                         "ignored when --reader names a preset")
    ap.add_argument("--reader-model", default="",
                    help="model id at the reader endpoint (defaults to --model)")
    ap.add_argument("--reader-key-env", default="",
                    help="env var holding the reader's API key "
                         "(default ZHIPUAI_API_KEY for glm, else OPENAI_API_KEY)")
    ap.add_argument("--reader-temperature", type=float, default=0.0,
                    help="sampling temperature for the channel-A reader. 0 by "
                         "default and it matters: an OpenAI-compatible endpoint "
                         "is sent no temperature at all unless one is set, and "
                         "Ollama then samples at 0.8 — two runs over the same "
                         "block crop returned materially different tables. "
                         "Channel G has had --notes-temperature since it was "
                         "written; this is the same guard one channel over")
    ap.add_argument("--reader-reasoning-effort", default="",
                    choices=["", "none", "low", "medium", "high"],
                    help="reasoning_effort for a hosted OpenAI-compatible channel-A "
                         "reader; 'none' switches Gemini's thinking off, as "
                         "--notes-reasoning-effort does for channel G")
    ap.add_argument("--reader-price", default="",
                    help="IN,OUT in USD per million tokens, e.g. 0.6,1.8 — makes "
                         "a non-Claude reader cost-comparable. Only the Claude "
                         "rates are known here, so this is asked for, not assumed")
    ap.add_argument("--notes-reader", default="glm",
                    choices=["claude", "openai-compatible", *READER_ENDPOINTS],
                    help="which model reads the below-table apparatus in channel G "
                         "(default glm: the apparatus is where the text layer "
                         "fails, and it is three crops a page)")
    ap.add_argument("--notes-model", default="",
                    help="model id for the channel-G reader — required, and not "
                         "guessed: OCR-capable vision model ids change often")
    ap.add_argument("--notes-key-env", default="",
                    help="env var holding the channel-G reader's API key")
    ap.add_argument("--notes-price", default="",
                    help="IN,OUT in USD per million tokens for the channel-G "
                         "reader, e.g. 0.6,1.8")
    ap.add_argument("--notes-regions", default="left,right,footer",
                    help="which crops of the apparatus to read; 'footer' alone "
                         "reads only the postal/railway legend")
    ap.add_argument("--list-models", action="store_true",
                    help="print the model ids the --notes-reader endpoint offers, "
                         "and exit")
    ap.add_argument("--probe", action="store_true",
                    help="send one real crop to the channel-G reader, print the "
                         "reply beside the text layer's reading of the same "
                         "region, report seconds per crop, and exit. Run this "
                         "first on any local model: a text-only one will answer "
                         "fluently without having seen the image")
    ap.add_argument("--probe-page", type=int, default=118,
                    help="which page the probe reads (default 118, whose footer "
                         "is the smallest crop in the volume). With "
                         "--notes-sections it probes that page's TALLEST section "
                         "of the requested kind, which is the case that decides "
                         "whether a reader can hold one at all")
    ap.add_argument("--notes-width", type=int, default=0,
                    help="cap the long edge of an apparatus crop, in pixels "
                         "(0 = the 2576px vision ceiling). Local vision models "
                         "usually work at 1024-1536 and downscale anything larger "
                         "themselves, unmeasured")
    ap.add_argument("--notes-sections", default="",
                    choices=["", "offices", "parts", "all"],
                    help="crop on the printed SECTION HEADINGS instead of on the "
                         "columns. 'offices' sends only the Úřady, ústavy "
                         "sections — the institution inventory — each as its own "
                         "image, with a prompt describing that one kind of entry "
                         "and only the symbols it prints. This is what makes a "
                         "small local model usable: a footnote column is ~1,350 x "
                         "1,000 px of six-point type and a 4-9B reader truncates "
                         "on it; a section is roughly half that. Replaces the "
                         "region crops, so the footer (postal legend) is not read "
                         "— run that as a separate pass")
    ap.add_argument("--notes-atlas", action="store_true",
                    help="send the printed symbol legend as a reference image "
                         "with every crop. The models can see this page but have "
                         "never seen its typeface's symbols drawn, and they agree "
                         "with each other on symbol identity only 9.5%% of the "
                         "time; this shows them the volume's own Vyklad znacek "
                         "plate instead of describing it in English. Needs "
                         "reference/places/symbols/atlas_prompt.png "
                         "(build_symbol_atlas.py) and raises the input by roughly "
                         "2,000 tokens a call, so --notes-num-ctx matters")
    ap.add_argument("--notes-save-sections", default="",
                    help="save every section crop the readers read, the page's own "
                         "pixels enlarged x2 under the gold's naming, with an index "
                         "(section_images.py) - what E3 and the Opus call cut from "
                         "beyond the gold (D-112)")
    ap.add_argument("--batch-prepare", default="",
                    help="queue each crop that is not in the cache as a request line in "
                         "this JSONL file instead of sending it (reader_batches.py submits "
                         "it and writes the replies into the cache; a second run then "
                         "reads every crop from the cache)")
    ap.add_argument("--notes-contrast", default="",
                    help="a sheet of look-alike symbols cut from the gold "
                         "(build_contrast_sheet.py, D-99), sent between the key "
                         "and every crop; needs --notes-atlas. Changes the prompt "
                         "and the crop cache key")
    ap.add_argument("--notes-num-ctx", type=int, default=0,
                    help="context window for a local reader (0 = the daemon's "
                         "default, which is 4096 regardless of what the model "
                         "supports). With --notes-atlas the input is ~4,600 "
                         "tokens, so leave this at 8192 or more or the daemon "
                         "silently drops the head of the prompt")
    ap.add_argument("--notes-max-height", type=int, default=0,
                    help="cut any crop taller than this many ALTO pixels into "
                         "strips, at real whitespace between printed lines. The "
                         "right control for sections, which vary from two lines "
                         "to twenty-five, where --notes-slices is a fixed count "
                         "that either leaves the long ones too big or dices the "
                         "short ones")
    ap.add_argument("--notes-slices", type=int, default=1,
                    help="cut each apparatus region into N horizontal strips, at "
                         "the whitespace between printed lines. Raises the pixels "
                         "per glyph a small local model sees, at N calls per "
                         "region instead of one")
    ap.add_argument("--notes-upscale", action="store_true",
                    help="blow each apparatus crop up to the vision ceiling. Off "
                         "by default: it roughly doubles the image tokens and adds "
                         "no detail the 399-DPI scan did not have")
    ap.add_argument("--notes-style", default="", choices=["", "annotate", "transcribe"],
                    help="annotate = transcribe and name every symbol from the "
                         "closed list; transcribe = text only, every symbol as "
                         "[?]. Default follows the model id: an OCR model gets "
                         "transcribe, a general vision model gets annotate")
    ap.add_argument("--notes-format", default="auto",
                    choices=["auto", "json", "text"],
                    help="how to read the reply. 'text' splits it on line breaks, "
                         "which is what a dedicated OCR model returns; 'json' "
                         "expects the lines schema. Default follows the model id")
    ap.add_argument("--notes-think", action="store_true",
                    help="let a local reasoning model think before answering. Off "
                         "by default and worth leaving off: on a transcription "
                         "prompt qwen3.5 spent its whole budget reasoning and "
                         "returned nothing at all")
    ap.add_argument("--notes-temperature", type=float, default=0.0,
                    help="sampling temperature for the channel-G reader. Default "
                         "0 — transcription is not a creative task, and a local "
                         "daemon samples at 0.8 unless told otherwise")
    ap.add_argument("--notes-reasoning-effort", default="",
                    choices=["", "none", "low", "medium", "high"],
                    help="reasoning_effort for a hosted OpenAI-compatible channel-G "
                         "reader. 'none' switches Gemini's thinking off; empty sends "
                         "nothing and the provider default applies — on Gemini 3.x "
                         "Flash that is thousands of billed thinking tokens a crop")
    ap.add_argument("--notes-label", default="",
                    help="suffix for this pass's output files, so two readers can "
                         "be run over the same pages without overwriting each "
                         "other (e.g. --notes-label glmocr)")
    ap.add_argument("--notes-max-tokens", type=int, default=4000)
    ap.add_argument("--no-crop-cache", action="store_true",
                    help="do not reuse crops already read. The cache is ON by "
                         "default and lives in <out>/crop_cache/<notes-label>/, "
                         "keyed by a hash of the crop bytes, the caption, the "
                         "model, the system prompt, the temperature and whether "
                         "the atlas was sent - so a change to any of those "
                         "invalidates on its own. It is what makes a long hosted "
                         "pass restartable at the crop rather than at the pass. "
                         "Pass this to force every crop to be read again, which "
                         "is what you want when the question is the reader's own "
                         "variance rather than its answer")
    ap.add_argument("--max-notes", type=int, default=0,
                    help="cap channel-G pages (0 = every page in the run)")
    ap.add_argument("--a-on-fail", action="store_true",
                    help="restrict channel A to the blocks that failed a "
                         "channel-B check: the escalation path, so the expensive "
                         "reader is spent only where the free one is known to be "
                         "wrong. The run reports what share that was")
    ap.add_argument("--effort", default="medium",
                    choices=["low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"])
    ap.add_argument("--thinking", default="adaptive",
                    choices=["adaptive", "disabled", "default"],
                    help="set explicitly: on Claude Opus 5 omitting it runs "
                         "adaptive, which costs output tokens on every block")
    ap.add_argument("--table-foot", default="rules", choices=["rules", "band"],
                    help="where channel B's table rows end: 'rules' (lexikon_1910 "
                         "0.2.0) at the foot of the column rules, where the "
                         "apparatus opens; 'band' at body_band's percentile foot, "
                         "as 0.1.0 did, for replaying a pass cached under it - "
                         "it loses the last rows on about half the table scans "
                         "and reads apparatus lines as rows on 22")
    ap.add_argument("--table-top", default="header", choices=["band", "header"],
                    help="where channel B's table rows start: 'header' (default "
                         "since lexikon_1910 0.4.0) just under the rule that "
                         "closes the column header; 'band' at body_band's top, as "
                         "before, for replaying a pass cached under it. 'header' "
                         "the rule that closes the column header, which reads 233 "
                         "more rows on 55 table scans (measure_table_top.py) and "
                         "changes those scans' block crops, so their cache misses")
    ap.add_argument("--geometry", default="image", choices=["image", "alto"],
                    help="where the apparatus section crops come from: 'image' "
                         "(default, lexikon_1910_notes 0.9.0) cuts them on the "
                         "page image's own columns and headings and labels each "
                         "with the text layer's heading, or with a vision read of "
                         "a heading only the image sees; strips are cut through "
                         "blank image rows. 'alto' is the text-layer geometry "
                         "of 0.8.x, kept as the comparison arm")
    ap.add_argument("--notes-legend", action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction,
                    default=True,
                    help="with --notes-sections, also read the footer band (the "
                         "postal and railway legend) from the image and resolve "
                         "the table's post and station keys against it; the text "
                         "layer's legend is kept as a cross-check")
    ap.add_argument("--okres-fold", action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction,
                    default=True,
                    help="read each page's okres off its running head with "
                         "lexikon_1910_names 0.2.0's folded matcher: Cyrillic "
                         "look-alikes folded, shape-fuzzy, ties refused, only the "
                         "political names the head prints. Changes the okres of "
                         "24 non-sealed table scans (measure_running_heads.py). "
                         "On by default since lexikon_1910_names 0.3.0; "
                         "--no-okres-fold is the exact lookup of before")
    ap.add_argument("--tiles", type=int, default=1,
                    help="split each block into N column tiles, each scaled to "
                         "the 2576px vision ceiling (1 = one crop, as before). "
                         "Columns 1-2 are repeated on every tile so rows align")
    ap.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=8000,
                    help="output cap per block; a truncated reply is reported as "
                         "such rather than as a generic failure")
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=4)
    ap.add_argument("--max-blocks", type=int, default=0,
                    help="cap channel-A calls (0 = every block on the pages)")
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true",
                    help="segment and price the run without calling the API")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=str(DEFAULT_OUT))
    args = ap.parse_args()

    if args.list_models:
        # The one thing this script will not guess is a model id, so it offers the
        # next best thing: ask the endpoint. Cheaper than a 404 on block one.
        base_url, key_env = READER_ENDPOINTS.get(
            args.notes_reader, (args.reader_url, "OPENAI_API_KEY"))
        from openai import OpenAI

        client = OpenAI(base_url=base_url,
                        api_key=os.environ.get(args.notes_key_env or key_env, ""))
        print(f"models at {base_url}:")
        for model in sorted(m.id for m in client.models.list()):
            print(f"  {model}")
        return 0

    if args.probe:
        try:
            abbreviations = lxin.load_abbreviations(
                ROOT / "reference" / "places" / "institution_abbreviations.csv",
                lang="cs")
        except Exception as exc:                        # noqa: BLE001
            print(f"abbreviation table unreadable: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
            return 1
        if args.notes_reader != "claude" and not args.notes_model:
            raise SystemExit("--probe needs --notes-model (or --notes-reader claude)")
        return probe_reader(args, abbreviations, page_number=args.probe_page)

    channels = {c.strip().upper() for c in args.channels.split(",") if c.strip()}
    pages = parse_pages(args.pages)
    # Validate before the grid fit and before any billed call: a malformed price
    # discovered after channel A has run is discovered after the money is spent.
    reader_price = parse_price(args.reader_price)
    parse_price(args.notes_price)
    # Same reason, one step earlier: channel G runs after the free channels, so a
    # missing model id discovered there throws away a completed channel-B run.
    if "G" in channels and args.notes_reader != "claude" and not args.notes_model:
        raise SystemExit(
            "--channels G needs --notes-model. This script does not guess a vision "
            "model id — run --list-models to see what the endpoint offers.")
    out_dir = Path(args.out)
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # ---- the grid -------------------------------------------------------- #
    alto_paths = sorted(CZ_PAGES.glob("*.alto.xml"))
    if not alto_paths:
        print(f"no ALTO files under {CZ_PAGES}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f"fitting the grid over {len(alto_paths)} pages ...")
    template, n_clean = lx.column_template(alto_paths)
    lx.write_grid_template(GRID_CSV, template, volume="cechy_1910_cz", n_pages=n_clean)
    print(f"  grid from {n_clean} pages with a complete rule set -> {GRID_CSV.name}")

    # ---- channel B ------------------------------------------------------- #
    print(f"\nchannel B (ALTO grid) over {len(pages)} pages ...")
    blocks_by_page: dict[str, list[lx.Block]] = {}
    pages_used: list[int] = []
    records: list[dict] = []
    geometry: list[dict] = []
    notes_list: list[lxnt.Notes] = []
    summaries: list[dict] = []
    # The district carries across page boundaries: a page that opens mid-okres
    # prints no summary row of its own, so without this every such page would
    # start unlabelled and fall back to the running head.
    okres_label = court_label = ""
    # The last block of the page before, held so the rows the next page prints
    # before its first municipality can be graded with it (lexikon_1910 0.5.0).
    held: tuple | None = None
    carried_blocks = 0
    for number in pages:
        path = CZ_PAGES / f"{number:04d}.alto.xml"
        if not path.exists():
            print(f"  {number:04d}: no ALTO file")
            continue
        try:
            page = lx.read_alto(path)
            _cols, observed = lx.fit_columns(page, template)
            rows = lx.extract_rows(page, template,
                                   foot_from_rules=args.table_foot == "rules",
                                   top_from_header=args.table_top == "header")
            blocks, orphans = lx.segment_blocks(rows, okres_label, court_label)
        except Exception as exc:                       # noqa: BLE001
            print(f"  {number:04d}: skipped — {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
            continue
        for kind, label, row in lx.summary_rows(rows):
            summaries.append({"page": page.stem, "kind": kind, "district": label,
                              "pop_total": row.get("pop_total"),
                              "houses": row.get("houses"),
                              "name": row.get("name")})
        if blocks:
            okres_label = blocks[-1].okres_label
            court_label = blocks[-1].court_label
        # The footnote apparatus sits below the band extract_rows reads, so it is
        # picked up here on the page object that is already open.
        notes = lxnt.extract_notes(page)
        if notes is not None:
            notes_list.append(notes)
        if not blocks:
            print(f"  {number:04d}: no municipality blocks")
            continue
        blocks_by_page[page.stem] = blocks
        pages_used.append(number)
        geometry.append({"page": page.stem, "boundaries_snapped_of_18": observed,
                         "rows": len(rows), "blocks": len(blocks),
                         "orphan_rows": len(orphans)})
        if held is not None and orphans and held[1] == number - 1:
            # A block split by a page break: its I4 sums are graded again with
            # the settlements printed overleaf. Only I4 changes — every row keeps
            # its own I1-I3 verdicts, and the I5 sequence is still per page.
            whole = lx.carry_block(held[0], orphans)
            records[:] = [r for r in records
                          if not (r.get("block_id") == whole.block_id
                                  and str(r.get("check", "")).startswith("I4_block"))]
            for col, (verdict, detail) in lx.grade_block_sum(whole).items():
                records.append({
                    "block_id": whole.block_id, "row_kind": "block",
                    "row_name": whole.name, "check": f"I4_block:{col}",
                    "verdict": verdict,
                    "detail": (detail + "; " if detail else "")
                              + f"{len(orphans)} rows carried from {page.stem}",
                    "channel": "B"})
            carried_blocks += 1
        for record in lx.grade_page(blocks):
            record["channel"] = "B"
            records.append(record)
        held = (blocks[-1], number)
    if carried_blocks:
        print(f"  {carried_blocks} blocks graded across a page break "
              f"(their settlements continue at the head of the next page)")
    total_blocks = sum(len(b) for b in blocks_by_page.values())
    print(f"  {len(pages_used)} pages, {total_blocks} municipality blocks")
    # Extrapolate from what this run actually segmented rather than from a stored
    # constant: a run over a district of small villages has a different blocks-per-
    # page than one over a city, and the volume figure should say which it came from.
    volume_blocks = (round(total_blocks / len(pages_used) * N_TABLE_PAGES)
                     if pages_used else VOLUME_BLOCKS)
    write_csv(out_dir / "geometry.csv", geometry)

    # ---- anchor the blocks to known municipalities ----------------------- #
    # Every block is matched against the obce its okres is known to contain, from
    # the project's own crosswalks. This is what makes the cross-volume join work
    # on badly OCR'd names, and it is the only check here that can see a block that
    # should not exist or a municipality that was lost — no arithmetic identity can.
    print("\nanchoring blocks to settlements_1910 ...")
    authority = lxnm.build_authority(ROOT / "data" / "final")
    heads = [(stem, lx.running_head(lx.read_alto(CZ_PAGES / f"{stem}.alto.xml")))
             for stem in sorted(blocks_by_page)]
    assignment = lxnm.assign_okresy(heads, authority, fold=args.okres_fold)
    sources = Counter(how for _id, how in assignment.values())
    print(f"  okres read from the running head on {sources['head']} pages"
          + (f" (+{sources['head_fuzzy']} fuzzy)" if args.okres_fold else "")
          + f", carried forward on {sources['carried']}, "
          f"unresolved on {sources['unresolved']}")

    # Blocks are assigned to the district *the register itself names above them*,
    # falling back to the running head only where no summary row has been seen yet
    # (the first page of a run opens mid-okres). A page is not a district: the
    # listing runs straight on, so at every boundary one page carries the end of
    # one okres and the start of the next, and a page-level assignment files the
    # neighbour's municipalities under the wrong district. On Kraslice that put
    # Krumlov's blocks in the totals and inflated every column by a fifth.
    cz_blocks_by_okres: dict[int, list[lx.Block]] = {}
    resolved_labels: dict[str, int | None] = {}
    label_sources = Counter()
    unresolved = 0
    for stem, blocks in blocks_by_page.items():
        page_okres, _how = assignment[stem]
        for block in blocks:
            label = block.okres_label
            okres_id = None
            if label:
                if label not in resolved_labels:
                    resolved_labels[label] = authority.resolve_okres(label)
                okres_id = resolved_labels[label]
                label_sources["summary row" if okres_id is not None
                              else "summary row unresolved → running head"] += 1
            else:
                label_sources["running head (no summary seen yet)"] += 1
            if okres_id is None:
                okres_id = page_okres
            if okres_id is None:
                unresolved += 1
                continue
            cz_blocks_by_okres.setdefault(okres_id, []).append(block)
    print("  block district from: "
          + "; ".join(f"{v} {k}" for k, v in label_sources.most_common()))
    if unresolved:
        print(f"  {unresolved} blocks — no district resolved, not anchored")
    write_csv(out_dir / "district_summaries.csv", summaries)

    cz_anchors: dict[int, list[lxnm.Anchor]] = {}
    anchor_rows: list[dict] = []
    expected_total = 0
    for okres_id, blocks in sorted(cz_blocks_by_okres.items()):
        candidates = authority.okres(okres_id)
        expected_total += len(candidates)
        anchors = lxnm.anchor_blocks(blocks, candidates)
        lxnm.harvest_printed_names(anchors, blocks)      # the volume names itself
        cz_anchors[okres_id] = anchors
        for anchor in anchors:
            anchor_rows.append({
                "block_id": anchor.block_id, "okres_id": okres_id,
                "printed_name": anchor.printed, "verdict": anchor.verdict,
                "obec": anchor.obec.cs_name if anchor.obec else "",
                "score": anchor.score, "runner_up": anchor.runner_up,
            })
    all_cz_anchors = [a for anchors in cz_anchors.values() for a in anchors]
    print(lxnm.anchor_report(all_cz_anchors, expected=expected_total,
                             label="Czech blocks"))
    write_csv(out_dir / "anchors.csv", anchor_rows)

    # ---- the footnote apparatus, from the text layer (free) --------------- #
    # The ``Části osad`` sections print every settlement's houses and population a
    # second time, broken into named parts. Different type, different part of the
    # page, so the OCR errors are uncorrelated with the table's — a fourth reading
    # channel that costs nothing and can repair cells the grid misread. The postal
    # legend keyed per *soudní* okres and the institution inventory come out of the
    # same pass, which is why blocks are grouped by court label here.
    print("\nfootnote apparatus (text layer) ...")
    all_blocks = [b for bs in blocks_by_page.values() for b in bs]
    blocks_by_court: dict[str, list[lx.Block]] = {}
    for blocks in blocks_by_page.values():
        for block in blocks:
            key = lxnt.normalise(block.court_label)
            if key:
                blocks_by_court.setdefault(key, []).append(block)
    try:
        abbreviations = lxin.load_abbreviations(
            ROOT / "reference" / "places" / "institution_abbreviations.csv",
            lang="cs")
    except Exception as exc:                            # noqa: BLE001
        print(f"  abbreviation table unreadable: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
        abbreviations = []
    records += apparatus_pass(notes_list, all_blocks, blocks_by_court,
                              abbreviations, out_dir)

    # ---- okres totals against the census (free) -------------------------- #
    # Every check above this line is internal to the page, and they share one blind
    # spot: none of them can see a municipality that was never emitted. Summing an
    # okres and comparing it to the census closes that, and only that.
    print("\nokres reconciliation against census_okres_1910 ...")
    census_findings: list[dict] = []
    try:
        import pandas as pd

        census = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data" / "final" / "census" /
                             "census_okres_1910.csv").set_index("okres_id")
        reconciliations = []
        for okres_id, blocks in sorted(cz_blocks_by_okres.items()):
            if okres_id not in census.index:
                print(f"  okres {okres_id}: no census row")
                continue
            row = census.loc[okres_id]
            expected = len(authority.okres(okres_id))
            anchors = cz_anchors.get(okres_id, [])
            matched_ids = {a.block_id for a in anchors if a.verdict == "matched"}
            # Sum only the blocks that anchored to an obec of *this* okres. A page
            # is assigned to one district, but districts change mid-page — the
            # register runs straight on — so a page-assigned set carries the
            # neighbouring okres's opening municipalities as well as its own. On
            # Kraslice that put Krumlov's blocks in the sum and inflated every
            # column by a fifth. Anchoring already knows which obec a block is;
            # this just believes it.
            kept = [b for b in blocks if b.block_id in matched_ids]
            rec = lxcs.reconcile(
                kept, row, okres_id=okres_id,
                okres_cs=str(row.get("okres_cs", "")),
                n_expected=expected,
                # Completeness is taken from the anchoring, not from the block
                # count: a page can carry blocks that matched no obec, and those
                # must not be allowed to stand in for the obce actually missing.
                n_found=len(matched_ids),
            )
            reconciliations.append(rec)
            census_findings += rec.findings
        for finding in census_findings:
            finding["channel"] = "census"
        records += census_findings
        write_csv(out_dir / "okres_reconciliation.csv", census_findings)
        print(lxcs.lexikon_1910_census_report(reconciliations))
    except Exception as exc:                            # noqa: BLE001
        print(f"  okres reconciliation failed: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")

    # ---- channel G — the apparatus, read from the image ------------------- #
    # Where the text layer stops paying. The table above reads at ~88% from the
    # ALTO; down here most of what is recorded is pictographic, and a pictogram the
    # OCR engine never identified is not a parsing problem. One call per crop,
    # three crops a page — against fifteen blocks a page for the table, which is
    # what makes reading the apparatus with a model and the table without one an
    # affordable combination rather than a compromise.
    if "G" in channels:
        print("\nchannel G (apparatus, vision) ...")
        try:
            from utils.lexikon_1910 import lexikon_1910_vision as lxv

            regions = tuple(r.strip() for r in args.notes_regions.split(",")
                            if r.strip())
            targets = [n for n in notes_list if n.page in blocks_by_page]
            if args.max_notes:
                targets = targets[:args.max_notes]
            allowed = lxv.vocabulary(abbreviations)
            crops_by_page: dict[str, list[tuple]] = {}
            region_counts = Counter()
            segments: list[lxnt.Segment] = []
            kinds = (("parts", "offices") if args.notes_sections == "all"
                     else (args.notes_sections,) if args.notes_sections else ())
            if kinds:
                # Targeted: cut on the printed headings, not on the columns. The
                # carry must walk *every* page in order — a section that opened
                # before this run's first page, or before a page the run skipped,
                # has no heading of its own and would otherwise lose its identity.
                target_pages = {n.page for n in targets}
                read_heading = None
                if args.geometry == "image" and not args.dry_run:
                    read_heading = heading_reader(args, abbreviations, out_dir)
                image_cuts: list = []
                printed_lines: dict = {}
                carry = None
                for notes in notes_list:
                    if notes.page in target_pages:
                        page = lx.read_alto(CZ_PAGES / f"{notes.page}.alto.xml")
                        image = lx.render_page(CZ_PDF, int(notes.page), page.width)
                        ink = None
                        legend_box = None
                        if args.geometry == "image":
                            cut, report = lxnt.image_section_segments(
                                notes, page, image, carry=carry,
                                read_heading=read_heading)
                            image_cuts.append(report)
                            ink, legend_box = report.ink, report.legend
                            trailing = lxnt.trailing_from_segments(cut, carry)
                        else:
                            cut = lxnt.section_segments(notes, page, carry=carry)
                            trailing = lxnt.trailing_section(notes, carry)
                        wanted = [s for s in cut if s.kind in kinds]
                        if args.notes_legend and notes.footer_lines is not None:
                            if legend_box is None:
                                legend_box = lxnt.notes_boxes(notes, page)["footer"]
                            wanted.append(lxnt.Segment(
                                kind="legend", district="", page=notes.page,
                                region="footer", box=legend_box, order=900,
                                lines=list(notes.footer_lines)))
                        crops = lxnt.crop_segments(
                            image, wanted, page,
                            target_width=args.notes_width or None,
                            upscale=args.notes_upscale, slices=args.notes_slices,
                            max_height=args.notes_max_height, ink=ink)
                        if args.notes_save_sections:
                            import section_images
                            section_images.save(image, wanted,
                                                Path(args.notes_save_sections))
                        if ink is not None:
                            printed_lines.update(
                                {(s.page, s.region, s.order):
                                 printed_line_count(ink, s.box, page.width)
                                 for s in wanted})
                        segments += wanted
                        crops_by_page[notes.page] = crops
                        for _crop, segment, _i, _n in crops:
                            region_counts[segment.kind] += 1
                        carry = trailing
                    else:
                        carry = lxnt.trailing_section(notes, carry)
                if image_cuts:
                    print(image_cut_report(image_cuts))
                heights = sorted(s.height for s in segments)
                if heights:
                    print(f"  {len(segments)} sections cut from "
                          f"{len(crops_by_page)} pages "
                          f"({', '.join(f'{sum(1 for s in segments if s.kind == k)} {k}' for k in kinds)}), "
                          f"median {heights[len(heights) // 2]} px tall, "
                          f"tallest {heights[-1]} px")
                    print(f"  -> {sum(len(c) for c in crops_by_page.values())} "
                          f"crops"
                          + (f" at --notes-max-height {args.notes_max_height}"
                             if args.notes_max_height else
                             "  (pass --notes-max-height to cut the tall ones "
                             "into strips)"))
                    if not args.notes_legend:
                        print("  the postal legend (the footer) is not read: "
                              "--no-notes-legend")
            else:
                for notes in targets:
                    page = lx.read_alto(CZ_PAGES / f"{notes.page}.alto.xml")
                    image = lx.render_page(CZ_PDF, int(notes.page), page.width)
                    crops = lxnt.crop_notes(image, notes, page, regions=regions,
                                            target_width=args.notes_width or None,
                                            upscale=args.notes_upscale,
                                            slices=args.notes_slices,
                                            max_height=args.notes_max_height)
                    crops_by_page[notes.page] = crops
                    for _crop, region in crops:
                        region_counts[region] += 1

            notes_price = parse_price(args.notes_price)
            if args.dry_run:
                # Priced from the crops that were actually cut, not from a guess at
                # the band's size: the apparatus is a third of a page on one sheet
                # and two lines on the next, and an average that ignores that is a
                # number with no error bar.
                import statistics

                tokens = [min(4784, job[0].width * job[0].height // 750)
                          for crops in crops_by_page.values() for job in crops]
                system_tokens = len(lxv.build_system(
                    abbreviations, section=kinds[0] if kinds else "",
                    atlas=args.notes_atlas, think=args.notes_think,
                    contrast=bool(args.notes_contrast))) // 4
                if tokens:
                    per_page = sum(tokens) / max(len(crops_by_page), 1)
                    print(f"  dry run — no API calls made")
                    print(f"  {len(crops_by_page)} pages, {sum(region_counts.values())} "
                          f"crops, median {int(statistics.median(tokens))} image "
                          f"tokens/crop ({per_page:.0f} per page)")
                    billing = ("cached, so a cache read on all but the first crop"
                               if args.notes_reader == "claude"
                               else "billed in full on every crop — an "
                                    "OpenAI-compatible endpoint has no prompt cache")
                    print(f"  the symbol legend makes the system prompt "
                          f"~{system_tokens} tokens, {billing}")
                    if notes_price:
                        est_in = (sum(tokens) / len(tokens) + system_tokens + 60)
                        per_crop = (est_in * notes_price[0]
                                    + 700 * notes_price[1]) / 1e6
                        # A targeted run's volume figure comes from the crops it
                        # actually cut, scaled by page count. The region form is a
                        # fixed three a page; a section form is not, and assuming
                        # it were would misprice the whole estimate.
                        n_volume = (round(sum(region_counts.values())
                                          / max(len(crops_by_page), 1)
                                          * N_TABLE_PAGES) if kinds else
                                    N_TABLE_PAGES * len(regions) * args.notes_slices)
                        print(f"  at {notes_price[0]}/{notes_price[1]} per Mtok: "
                              f"${per_crop * sum(region_counts.values()):.2f} for "
                              f"these crops, ${per_crop * n_volume:,.0f} for the "
                              f"whole Čechy volume ({n_volume:,} crops)")
                    else:
                        print("  pass --notes-price IN,OUT to price it")
            else:
                # One reader per section kind: the prompt describes that kind's
                # entries and lists only its symbols, so a run over both cannot
                # share one system prompt. Off the targeted path there is one
                # reader and one prompt, as before.
                atlas_image = None
                if args.notes_atlas:
                    from PIL import Image as _Image

                    atlas_path = (ROOT / "reference" / "places" / "symbols"
                                  / "atlas_prompt.png")
                    if not atlas_path.exists():
                        raise SystemExit(
                            f"--notes-atlas needs {atlas_path}; build it with "
                            f"python utils/lexikon_1910/build_symbol_atlas.py")
                    atlas_image = _Image.open(atlas_path).convert("RGB")
                    print(f"  symbol key: {atlas_path.name} "
                          f"({atlas_image.width}x{atlas_image.height}) sent with "
                          f"every crop")
                contrast_image, contrast_digest = None, ""
                if args.notes_contrast:
                    import hashlib as _hashlib
                    from PIL import Image as _Image

                    contrast_path = Path(args.notes_contrast)
                    if atlas_image is None or not contrast_path.exists():
                        raise SystemExit(
                            f"--notes-contrast needs --notes-atlas and {contrast_path} "
                            f"(python utils/lexikon_1910/build_contrast_sheet.py)")
                    contrast_image = _Image.open(contrast_path).convert("RGB")
                    contrast_digest = _hashlib.sha256(
                        contrast_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16]
                    print(f"  contrast sheet: {contrast_path.name} "
                          f"({contrast_image.width}x{contrast_image.height}, "
                          f"{contrast_digest}) sent after the key")
                readers = {kind: build_notes_reader(args, abbreviations,
                                                    section=kind, quiet=i > 0)
                           for i, kind in enumerate(kinds)} or \
                          {"": build_notes_reader(args, abbreviations)}
                if kinds and any(s.kind == "legend" for s in segments):
                    # The legend is no section: the general prompt, which
                    # describes the footer as well as the two sections.
                    readers["legend"] = build_notes_reader(args, abbreviations,
                                                           quiet=True)
                reader = next(iter(readers.values()))
                print(f"  reader: {reader.name} ({args.notes_model or args.model})")
                if atlas_image is not None:
                    # The atlas leads every request of the pass unchanged, so a
                    # reader that has a prompt cache keeps it there.
                    for picked in readers.values():
                        if hasattr(picked, "shared_parts"):
                            picked.shared_parts = 2 if contrast_image is not None else 1
                if args.notes_reader == "ollama" and args.workers > 1:
                    # Ollama serialises requests unless OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL is set,
                    # so extra workers queue rather than overlap — harmless, but
                    # the run looks concurrent while it is not, and one 12 GB card
                    # will not hold two copies of a 9B vision model anyway.
                    print(f"  note: --workers {args.workers} against a local "
                          f"daemon queues unless OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL is set")

                # PARKED, NOT RETRIED. Once the endpoint says the quota is spent,
                # every remaining crop of this pass returns without a request:
                # the limit is a property of the account and the window, not of
                # the crop, so the next call would spend a request to be told the
                # same thing — and on a metered plan a refusal can itself count.
                # `parked` is the evidence the pass was cut short rather than
                # read badly, and it is what stops the result being scored.
                parked: dict = {"at": None, "error": "", "retry_after": None,
                                "done_before": 0, "skipped": 0, "status": None,
                                "from_cache": 0}
                parked_lock = threading.Lock()

                # --- the crop cache ------------------------------------- #
                # A four-hour hosted pass that dies at crop 2,400 returns
                # NOTHING: `as_completed` collects, and a process that is gone
                # collects nothing. This is the same rule bakeoff.py already
                # applies one level up - "a pass whose inventory_<label>.csv
                # already exists is skipped" - moved down from the pass to the
                # crop.
                #
                # SCOPED PER LABEL, and that is not tidiness. The key below is a
                # content hash, so two passes issuing byte-identical requests
                # would share an entry - which is exactly what the `again`
                # variant must NOT do. `again` is `base` re-run to measure the
                # run-to-run noise floor at temperature 0; served from base's
                # cache it would report 0.000 by construction instead of by
                # measurement, and the bake-off would lose the one number that
                # tells it whether any other difference is evidence.
                #
                # The hash covers the crop bytes, the caption, the model, the
                # system prompt, the temperature and whether the atlas was sent,
                # so changing geometry, prompt, atlas or model invalidates on its
                # own rather than quietly serving the old answer.
                cache_dir = None
                if not args.no_crop_cache:
                    cache_dir = (out_dir / "crop_cache"
                                 / (args.notes_label or "unlabelled"))
                    cache_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

                def cache_key(crop, caption: str, kind: str) -> str:
                    picked = readers[kind]
                    h = hashlib.sha256()
                    parts = [encode_png(crop), caption,
                             str(getattr(picked, "model", "")),
                             str(getattr(picked, "system", "")),
                             str(getattr(picked, "temperature", "")),
                             "atlas" if atlas_image is not None else "bare"]
                    # Appended ONLY when set, so every key written before the flag
                    # existed stays byte-identical and its cache keeps serving —
                    # while a thinking-off reading can never be served a
                    # thinking-on answer, or the reverse.
                    effort = getattr(picked, "reasoning_effort", None)
                    if effort:
                        parts.append(f"reasoning_effort={effort}")
                    if contrast_digest:
                        parts.append(f"contrast={contrast_digest}")
                    for part in parts:
                        h.update(part.encode("utf-8"))
                        h.update(bytes(1))          # a separator, so fields cannot run together
                    return h.hexdigest()

                def read_crop(job):
                    slot, crop, caption, kind = job
                    picked = readers[kind]
                    # Ahead of the parked check on purpose: a cache hit costs no
                    # request, so a parked pass can still finish from what it
                    # already read rather than skipping crops it has answers for.
                    key = cache_key(crop, caption, kind) if cache_dir else None
                    if key:
                        hit = cache_dir / f"{key}.json"
                        if hit.exists():
                            try:
                                rec = json.loads(hit.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
                            except (ValueError, OSError):
                                rec = None          # corrupt entry: read it again
                            if rec is not None:
                                with parked_lock:
                                    parked["from_cache"] += 1
                                return slot, rec["lines"], rec["usage"]
                    with parked_lock:
                        if parked["at"] is not None:
                            parked["skipped"] += 1
                            return slot, None, {"error": "parked: rate limited"}
                    # The key first, the page second — the prompt refers to
                    # them in that order, and a reader that takes images
                    # positionally must not be told the page is the key.
                    payload = ([(atlas_image, "This image is the key: every "
                                              "printed symbol of this volume and "
                                              "its token.")]
                               if atlas_image is not None else []) + \
                              ([(contrast_image, "This image sets look-alike "
                                                 "symbols side by side, cut from "
                                                 "other pages of this volume.")]
                               if contrast_image is not None else []) + \
                              [(crop, caption)]
                    if args.batch_prepare and key:
                        if hasattr(picked, "params"):
                            request = picked.params(payload, "Transcribe this image.")
                        elif hasattr(picked, "body"):
                            request = picked.body(payload, "Transcribe this image.")
                        else:
                            request = None
                        if request is not None:
                            line = json.dumps({"key": key, "reader": picked.name,
                                               "cache_dir": str(cache_dir),
                                               "slot": list(slot), "kind": kind,
                                               "model": getattr(picked, "model", ""),
                                               "request": request})
                            with parked_lock:
                                with open(args.batch_prepare, "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                                    fh.write(line + "\n")
                            return slot, None, {"error": "batched: queued"}
                    for attempt in range(3):
                        try:
                            lines, usage = picked(payload,
                                                  "Transcribe this image.")
                            # SUCCESSES ONLY. A failure is never cached: a
                            # transient rate limit or a truncated reply would
                            # otherwise be frozen into the pass permanently, and
                            # every later run would inherit it without a request
                            # that could have gone the other way. An EMPTY but
                            # well-formed reply IS cached - at temperature 0 the
                            # retry returns the same nothing, and the code below
                            # already treats that as an answer rather than a gap.
                            if key:
                                try:
                                    tmp = cache_dir / f"{key}.json.part"
                                    tmp.write_text(json.dumps(
                                        {"lines": lines, "usage": usage,
                                         "slot": list(slot), "kind": kind,
                                         "model": getattr(picked, "model", ""),
                                         "at": time.time()}), encoding="utf-8")
                                    tmp.replace(cache_dir / f"{key}.json")
                                except (TypeError, ValueError, OSError):
                                    pass            # a pass must not die on its cache
                            with parked_lock:
                                parked["done_before"] += 1
                            return slot, lines, usage
                        except Truncated:
                            if hasattr(picked, "max_tokens"):
                                picked.max_tokens = min(picked.max_tokens * 2, 32000)
                            if attempt == 2:
                                return slot, None, {"error": "truncated"}
                        except RateLimited as exc:
                            with parked_lock:
                                if parked["at"] is None:
                                    parked.update(
                                        at=time.time(), error=str(exc),
                                        retry_after=exc.retry_after,
                                        status=exc.status)
                                    print(f"\n  !! RATE LIMITED after "
                                          f"{parked['done_before']} crops: "
                                          f"{str(exc)[:120]}")
                                    print(f"     parking this model — the rest "
                                          f"of the matrix still runs.")
                                parked["skipped"] += 1
                            return slot, None, {"error": f"rate limited: {exc}"}
                        except Exception as exc:        # noqa: BLE001
                            if attempt == 2:
                                return slot, None, {"error": str(exc)}
                            time.sleep(2 * (attempt + 1))

                if kinds:
                    # The slot is the segment, so strips of one section come back
                    # under the section they were cut from. The district is
                    # deliberately **not** in the caption: the model is told where
                    # in the crop it is, never what the crop is supposed to say.
                    jobs = [((segment.page, segment.region, segment.order), crop,
                             ("This image is the postal and railway legend printed "
                              "under the footnote apparatus." if segment.kind == "legend"
                              else f"This image is one section of the footnote "
                              f"apparatus." if n == 1 else
                              f"This image is part {i + 1} of {n} of one section "
                              f"of the footnote apparatus, in printed order."),
                             segment.kind)
                            for crops in crops_by_page.values()
                            for crop, segment, i, n in crops]
                    segment_by_slot = {(s.page, s.region, s.order): s
                                       for s in segments}
                else:
                    jobs = [((stem, region, i), crop,
                             f"This image is the {region} region of the footnote "
                             f"apparatus.", "")
                            for stem, crops in crops_by_page.items()
                            for i, (crop, region) in enumerate(crops)]
                    segment_by_slot = {}
                started = time.time()
                with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=args.workers) as pool:
                    # `as_completed`, not `pool.map`. map yields in SUBMISSION
                    # order, so nothing can be reported until the last crop is
                    # back. Every result carries its own slot and the consumer
                    # below is keyed by it, so completion order is free to differ
                    # from submission order — the output is identical, only the
                    # silence is gone.
                    futures = {pool.submit(read_crop, job): k
                               for k, job in enumerate(jobs)}
                    arrived = []
                    for done, future in enumerate(as_completed(futures), 1):
                        arrived.append((futures[future], future.result()))
                        if done % PROGRESS_EVERY == 0 or done == len(futures):
                            each = (time.time() - started) / done
                            left = each * (len(futures) - done) / 60
                            print(f"    {done}/{len(futures)} crops — "
                                  f"{each:.1f}s each, ~{left:.0f} min left",
                                  flush=True)
                # BACK INTO SUBMISSION ORDER before anything is assembled. The note
                # above was true of distinct slots and false of strips: the strips
                # of one tall section share its slot, and they were concatenated
                # below in the order they *finished*. With four workers a section's
                # second strip regularly beat its first, its entries landed under
                # the wrong municipality, and the same cached answers scored
                # differently live and on replay (E1, 2026-09-22: one pass 279
                # claims live, 285 replayed). Jobs are built in printed order, so
                # their index is the reading order.
                results = [result for _k, result in
                           sorted(arrived, key=lambda pair: pair[0])]
                g_elapsed = time.time() - started
                if cache_dir is not None and parked["from_cache"]:
                    # Said plainly, because the token counts below do NOT
                    # separate the two: they are the cost of the PASS, and the
                    # cached share of it was billed on an earlier run.
                    print(f"    {parked['from_cache']}/{len(jobs)} crops served "
                          f"from crop_cache/{cache_dir.name}/ — no request was "
                          f"made for those, and their tokens below were paid for "
                          f"on an earlier run, not this one")

                g_usage = Counter()
                rejected_total = Counter()
                repeats_total = 0
                g_empty: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
                lines_by_page: dict[str, dict[str, list[str]]] = {}
                lines_by_slot: dict[tuple, list[str]] = {}
                g_failures = 0
                for slot, lines, usage in results:
                    page_stem, region, _order = slot
                    for key in ("input", "output", "cache_write", "cache_read"):
                        g_usage[key] += usage.get(key, 0)
                    if lines is None:
                        g_failures += 1
                        continue
                    if not lines:
                        # A well-formed reply with nothing in it. This is *not* the
                        # same as a failure and must not be counted as a success
                        # either: the model was shown a crop with print on it and
                        # returned no lines, and at temperature 0 a retry returns
                        # the same nothing. Silence here reads downstream as "this
                        # region of the page was blank", which is a lie about the
                        # source rather than a gap in the run.
                        g_empty.append((page_stem, region))
                        continue
                    # The closed-set guard runs before anything downstream sees the
                    # text: a token nobody curated must not reach the decoder, where
                    # it would either be dropped in silence or — worse — matched by
                    # a shorter code nested inside it.
                    deduped, repeats = lxv.drop_repeats(
                        [str(line) for line in lines])
                    repeats_total += repeats
                    clean, rejected = lxv.guard_tokens(deduped, allowed)
                    rejected_total += rejected
                    # Strips of one crop arrive as separate results and are
                    # concatenated in job order — restored above, because
                    # `as_completed` does not preserve it — since a region or a
                    # section cut into strips has to come back as one flow or its
                    # entries stop lining up with their keys.
                    lines_by_slot.setdefault(slot, []).extend(clean)
                    lines_by_page.setdefault(page_stem, {}).setdefault(
                        region, []).extend(clean)
                n_crops = len(jobs)
                rate = n_crops / g_elapsed if g_elapsed else 0
                print(f"  {len(lines_by_page)} pages read, {g_failures} crops "
                      f"failed, {g_elapsed:.0f}s ({rate:.2f} crops/s)")
                # THE MARKER IS THE POINT OF ALL THIS. Without it the pass exits
                # 0, writes an inventory, and is scored — a limit hit at crop
                # three is then reported as a model that read the volume badly.
                # The file says otherwise, and `bakeoff.run_matrix` reads it to
                # mark the pass INCOMPLETE and to park the model for the rest of
                # the night.
                if parked["at"] is not None:
                    done = parked["done_before"]
                    before = parked["at"] - started
                    # Its OWN suffix. The shared `label` is not bound until the
                    # decode block further down, so reading it here would have
                    # picked up whatever `label` last held in an enclosing scope
                    # — a district name, from the block loop — and written the
                    # marker somewhere nothing looks for it.
                    marker_suffix = (f"_{args.notes_label}"
                                     if args.notes_label else "_vision")
                    marker = {
                        "label": args.notes_label or "G",
                        "model": args.notes_model or args.model,
                        "sections": args.notes_sections,
                        "atlas": bool(args.notes_atlas),
                        "contrast": args.notes_contrast or "",
                        "crops_total": n_crops,
                        "crops_done_before_limit": done,
                        "crops_skipped": parked["skipped"],
                        "seconds_before_limit": round(before, 1),
                        # Requests per second up to the refusal. This is the only
                        # honest rate: after it, nothing was sent.
                        "crops_per_second_before_limit":
                            round(done / before, 4) if before > 0 else None,
                        "status": parked["status"],
                        "error": parked["error"],
                        # The server's own number, or null. NEVER guessed — it is
                        # the only evidence of how wide the window is, and the
