                        # full-sweep projection is built on it.
                        "retry_after_seconds": parked["retry_after"],
                        "limit_at": time.strftime(
                            "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", time.localtime(parked["at"])),
                        "started": time.strftime(
                            "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", time.localtime(started)),
                    }
                    write_json(out_dir / f"ratelimit{marker_suffix}.json",
                               marker)
                    print(f"  !! PASS INCOMPLETE — {done} of {n_crops} crops "
                          f"read before the limit, {parked['skipped']} parked")
                    print(f"     marker: ratelimit{marker_suffix}.json")
                if g_empty:
                    where = ", ".join(f"{p}/{r}" for p, r in g_empty[:6])
                    print(f"  !! {len(g_empty)} crops returned a well-formed reply "
                          f"with NO lines: {where}"
                          + (" ..." if len(g_empty) > 6 else ""))
                    print(f"     Print was on those crops. Downstream this looks "
                          f"like a blank region, not a gap — treat the affected "
                          f"pages as unread.")
                if rate:
                    # The number that decides a local run. Money is not the
                    # constraint on a daemon of one's own; the calendar is. A
                    # targeted run's volume figure comes from its own crops per
                    # page, because sections are not three a page.
                    n_volume = (round(n_crops / max(len(crops_by_page), 1)
                                      * N_TABLE_PAGES) if kinds else
                                N_TABLE_PAGES * len(regions) * args.notes_slices)
                    print(f"  at this rate the whole Čechy apparatus "
                          f"({n_volume:,} crops) is ~{n_volume / rate / 3600:.1f} h")

                # One suffix for every artefact of this pass, so a second reader
                # over the same pages sits beside the first instead of on top of
                # it. Two readings that overwrite each other cannot be compared,
                # and comparing them is the entire reason to run two.
                label = f"_{args.notes_label}" if args.notes_label else "_vision"
                by_page = {n.page: n for n in notes_list}
                vision_notes = [
                    lxv.notes_from_regions(stem, lines, by_page.get(stem))
                    for stem, lines in sorted(lines_by_page.items())]
                write_csv(out_dir / f"notes{label}.csv",
                          [{"page": n.page, "region": region, "line_no": i, "text": line}
                           for n in vision_notes
                           for region, lines in (("left", n.left_lines),
                                                 ("right", n.right_lines),
                                                 ("footer", n.footer_lines))
                           for i, line in enumerate(lines)])

                print("\n  --- the same consumers, on the image read")
                prefix = f"{args.notes_label or 'G'}:"
                if kinds:
                    # Targeted: the sections are the unit, so they are assembled
                    # from the segments rather than re-cut out of a Notes the
                    # crops never formed. Both channels go through the same
                    # assembly, so a difference between them is a difference in
                    # the reading and not in the wiring.
                    # Sorted on the segment's own reading-order index, not on the
                    # slot tuple: "left" sorting before "right" is an accident of
                    # the alphabet, and the order the sections come back in is
                    # what decides which entries land under which heading.
                    read = [(segment_by_slot[slot], lines)
                            for slot, lines in sorted(
                                lines_by_slot.items(),
                                key=lambda kv: (kv[0][0], kv[0][2]))
                            if segment_by_slot[slot].kind != "legend"]
                    vision_sections = lxv.sections_from_segments(read)
                    alto_sections = lxv.sections_from_segments(
                        [(s, s.lines) for s in segments if s.kind != "legend"])
                    legend_lines = {slot[0]: lines
                                    for slot, lines in lines_by_slot.items()
                                    if segment_by_slot[slot].kind == "legend"}
                    write_csv(out_dir / f"crop_audit{label}.csv",
                              crop_audit(lines_by_slot, segment_by_slot,
                                         printed_lines))
                    if legend_lines:
                        records += legend_pass(legend_lines, notes_list,
                                               all_blocks, blocks_by_court,
                                               abbreviations, out_dir, prefix,
                                               label)
                    consumers = tuple(c for c in ("parts", "institutions")
                                      if c != "parts" or "parts" in kinds)
                    g_records = apparatus_pass(
                        [], all_blocks, blocks_by_court, abbreviations, out_dir,
                        prefix=prefix, suffix=label, sections=vision_sections,
                        consumers=consumers)
                    records += g_records

                    # I11 — the join this whole pass exists for. The text layer
                    # knows where every marker is; the image read knows what it is.
                    b_records, _b_entries = lxin.decode_sections(
                        alto_sections, abbreviations)
                    # A transcription pass names nothing by design, so its
                    # placeholders are counted as markers-seen instead — otherwise
                    # the control cannot report on the one thing it exists to test.
                    joined = lxin.join_symbols(
                        b_records, g_records,
                        count_unnamed=getattr(reader, "prompt_style", "")
                        == "transcribe")
                    for record in joined:
                        record["channel"] = f"{args.notes_label or 'G'}+B"
                    records += joined
                    write_csv(out_dir / f"symbol_join{label}.csv", joined)
                    print()
                    print(lxin.lexikon_1910_join_report(joined))

                    # I13 — the inventory the pipeline should actually use. The
                    # image read is the record here and the text layer corroborates
                    # it, because the text layer is not a complete locator of the
                    # markers: it emits roughly a third of what is printed, and
                    # which third depends on how the OCR happened to fail.
                    inventory = lxin.build_inventory(g_records, b_records)
                    for row in inventory:
                        row["channel"] = f"{args.notes_label or 'G'}>B"
                    records += inventory
                    # I14 — the entry keys are the table's own bold and
                    # light sequence numbers, so the inventory can carry the name
                    # of the place each institution belonged to.
                    lxin.attach_places(inventory,
                                       lxin.place_index(blocks_by_court))
                    write_csv(out_dir / f"inventory{label}.csv", inventory)
                    print()
                    print(lxin.lexikon_1910_inventory_report(inventory))
                    print()
                    print(lxin.lexikon_1910_places_joined_report(inventory))

                    agreement = (lxv.compare_sections(alto_sections,
                                                      vision_sections)
                                 + lxv.symbols_check_sections(alto_sections,
                                                              vision_sections)
                                 + lxv.content_check(alto_sections,
                                                   vision_sections))
                    invented = [f for f in agreement
                                if f["verdict"] == "invented"]
                    if invented:
                        print()
                        print(f"  !! {len(invented)} of "
                              f"{sum(1 for f in agreement if f['check'] == 'G_content')} "
                              f"sections came back with the format of the print "
                              f"and not its words.")
                        print(f"     A reader that is not reading answers "
                              f"fluently. Do not use this pass.")
                        for finding in invented[:3]:
                            print(f"     {finding['page']} "
                                  f"{finding['district']}: {finding['detail']}")
                else:
                    g_records = apparatus_pass(vision_notes, all_blocks,
                                               blocks_by_court, abbreviations,
                                               out_dir, prefix=prefix,
                                               suffix=label)
                    records += g_records
                    agreement = (lxv.compare_notes(notes_list, vision_notes)
                                 + lxv.symbols_check(notes_list, vision_notes))
                for finding in agreement:
                    finding["channel"] = f"{args.notes_label or 'G'}|B"
                records += agreement
                print()
                print(lxv.lexikon_1910_vision_report(
                    len(lines_by_page), region_counts, rejected_total, agreement,
                    resolved=[r for r in g_records
                              if r.get("channel") == f"{prefix}institutions"],
                    repeats=repeats_total, targeted=bool(kinds)))
                if notes_price:
                    # `input` is what the API billed in full; cached tokens are
                    # counted beside it, and leaving them out priced a Claude
                    # pass as though its system prompt had been free.
                    billed_in = (g_usage["input"]
                                 + CACHE_WRITE_RATE * g_usage["cache_write"]
                                 + CACHE_READ_RATE * g_usage["cache_read"])
                    cost = (billed_in * notes_price[0]
                            + g_usage["output"] * notes_price[1]) / 1e6
                    per_page = cost / max(len(lines_by_page), 1)
                    print(f"  cost: ${cost:.2f}  (${per_page:.4f}/page, "
                          f"${per_page * N_TABLE_PAGES:,.0f} for the volume)")
                else:
                    print(f"  tokens: {g_usage['input']:,} in, "
                          f"{g_usage['output']:,} out — pass --notes-price IN,OUT "
                          f"to price them")
        except Exception as exc:                        # noqa: BLE001
            print(f"  channel G failed: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")

    # ---- channel A ------------------------------------------------------- #
    a_blocks: dict[str, lx.Block] = {}
    #: Every row the reader returned, before ``rows_to_block`` keeps only the
    #: first block — what the table scorer compares with the gold.
    a_raw: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
    usage_total = Counter()
    elapsed = 0.0
    escalation_share = 1.0
    if "A" in channels:
        targets = [(stem, block) for stem, blocks in blocks_by_page.items()
                   for block in blocks]
        if args.a_on_fail:
            # The escalation path. Channel B grades itself, so the blocks it got
            # wrong are already known by the time this runs — and they are the only
            # blocks where a second, billed reading buys anything. Re-reading the
            # ~88% that already satisfy the invariants pays for confirmation of
            # what is not in doubt.
            failed = {r["block_id"] for r in records
                      if r.get("channel") == "B"
                      and r.get("verdict") in ("fail", "unparseable")}
            n_all = len(targets)
            targets = [(s, b) for s, b in targets if b.block_id in failed]
            # The share is carried into the volume extrapolation below, because
            # "$X for every block" is the wrong number once only the failures are
            # being read — and the wrong number in the expensive direction.
            escalation_share = len(targets) / n_all if n_all else 1.0
            graded = [r for r in records if r.get("channel") == "B"
                      and r.get("verdict") in ("pass", "fail", "unparseable")]
            bad = sum(1 for r in graded if r["verdict"] != "pass")
            print(f"\n--a-on-fail: {len(targets)} of {n_all} blocks "
                  f"({escalation_share:.0%}) failed a channel-B check and will be "
                  f"re-read. A block escalates if *any* of its rows fails *any* "
                  f"check, so the block share is far above the "
                  f"{bad / len(graded):.0%} of individual checks that failed")
        if args.max_blocks:
            targets = targets[:args.max_blocks]
        rate_in, rate_out = PRICING[args.model]
        if args.reader != "claude" and reader_price:
            # The dry run prices with these; a hosted reader is not --model.
            rate_in, rate_out = reader_price
        print(f"\nchannel A (vision, "
              f"{args.model if args.reader == 'claude' else args.reader_model}, "
              f"effort={args.effort}): "
              f"{len(targets)} blocks")
        if args.dry_run:
            # Measure the crops rather than guessing at them: a block is a thin
            # strip (~2670 x 120 px), so the image cost is an order of magnitude
            # below a whole-page read and the estimate should say so from the
            # actual geometry.
            import statistics

            sample = targets[:60]
            image_tokens: list[int] = []
            rendered: dict[str, tuple] = {}
            for stem, block in sample:
                if stem not in rendered:
                    page = lx.read_alto(CZ_PAGES / f"{stem}.alto.xml")
                    rendered[stem] = (page, lx.render_page(CZ_PDF, int(stem), page.width))
                page, image = rendered[stem]
                tiles = lx.tile_block(image, page, block, template,
                                      tiles=args.tiles)
                # Anthropic bills roughly (w x h)/750 tokens, capped at the
                # high-resolution ceiling. Summed over the tiles actually sent.
                image_tokens.append(sum(min(4784, t.width * t.height // 750)
                                        for t, _f, _l in tiles))
            median_image = int(statistics.median(image_tokens))
            # System prompt is cached, so it is a cache *read* on all but the first
            # call. The output figure has to include **thinking**: on Claude Opus 5
            # thinking is on unless disabled, it is billed at the output rate, and
            # leaving it out of the estimate understated the volume by a multiple.
            est_json = 600
            est_thinking = 0 if args.thinking == "disabled" else THINKING_TOKENS.get(
                args.effort, 800)
            est_in, est_cached, est_out = (median_image + 40, 900,
                                           est_json + est_thinking)
            per_block = (est_in * rate_in
                         + est_cached * rate_in * 0.1
                         + est_out * rate_out) / 1e6
            print("  dry run — no API calls made")
            print(f"  measured crops ({args.tiles} tile(s)/block): "
                  f"median {median_image} image tokens "
                  f"(min {min(image_tokens)}, max {max(image_tokens)})")
            print(f"  thinking: {args.thinking}"
                  + (f" (~{est_thinking} tokens/block assumed at effort "
                     f"{args.effort}, billed as output)" if est_thinking else ""))
            print(f"  estimate at {est_in} in + {est_cached} cached + "
                  f"{est_out} out per block: ${per_block * len(targets):.2f} "
                  f"for these {len(targets)} blocks (${per_block:.4f}/block)")
            n_volume = volume_blocks * escalation_share
            scope = ("the blocks that would escalate across the volume"
                     if args.a_on_fail else "the whole Čechy volume")
            print(f"  extrapolated to {scope} (~{n_volume:,.0f} blocks): "
                  f"${per_block * n_volume:,.0f}, or "
                  f"${per_block * n_volume / 2:,.0f} on the Batches API")
            # The estimate above bills the system prompt at the cache-read rate on
            # all but the first call. That only happens if it clears the model's
            # minimum cacheable prefix — below it, caching fails silently and every
            # block pays the full input rate instead of a tenth.
            minimum = CACHE_MINIMUM.get(args.model)
            if minimum and est_cached < minimum:
                uncached = (est_in + est_cached) * rate_in + est_out * rate_out
                print(f"  ! the ~{est_cached}-token system prompt is under "
                      f"{args.model}'s {minimum}-token cache minimum, so it may not "
                      f"cache at all — worst case ${uncached / 1e6 * len(targets):.2f} "
                      f"for these blocks, ${uncached / 1e6 * volume_blocks:,.0f} for the volume. "
                      f"Check usage.cache_read_input_tokens on the real run.")
        else:
            reader = build_reader(args)
            print(f"  reader: {reader.name}")
            pages_cache: dict[str, tuple] = {}
            for stem in blocks_by_page:
                page = lx.read_alto(CZ_PAGES / f"{stem}.alto.xml")
                image = lx.render_page(CZ_PDF, int(stem), page.width)
                pages_cache[stem] = (page, image)

            # A CACHE FOR THE TABLE TOO (D-115), keyed like the notes' crop cache:
            # the tiles' bytes and captions, the instruction, the model, the prompt
            # and every thinking setting. It is what lets the table be batched: a
            # run with --batch-prepare queues each uncached block instead of
            # sending it, reader_batches.py writes the replies here, and the next
            # run reads every block from the cache.
            table_cache = None
            if not args.no_crop_cache:
                table_cache = (out_dir / "table_cache"
                               / (args.notes_label or "unlabelled"))
                table_cache.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            table_lock = threading.Lock()

            def table_key(parts, instruction: str) -> str:
                h = hashlib.sha256()
                for piece in ([encode_png(im) + "\0" + cap for im, cap in parts]
                              + [instruction, str(getattr(reader, "model", "")),
                                 str(getattr(reader, "system", "")),
                                 str(getattr(reader, "temperature", "")),
                                 str(getattr(reader, "reasoning_effort", "") or ""),
                                 str(getattr(reader, "thinking", "")),
                                 str(getattr(reader, "effort", ""))]):
                    h.update(piece.encode("utf-8"))
                    h.update(bytes(1))
                return h.hexdigest()

            def run(job):
                stem, block = job
                page, image = pages_cache[stem]
                tiles = lx.tile_block(image, page, block, template,
                                      tiles=args.tiles)
                parts, instruction = block_parts(tiles)
                key = table_key(parts, instruction) if table_cache else None
                hit = table_cache / f"{key}.json" if key else None
                if hit is not None and hit.exists():
                    record = json.loads(hit.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
                    return stem, block, record["lines"], record.get("usage", {})
                if args.batch_prepare and hit is not None:
                    make = getattr(reader, "params", None) or getattr(reader, "body", None)
                    if make is not None:
                        line = json.dumps({"key": key, "reader": reader.name,
                                           "cache_dir": str(table_cache),
                                           "slot": [stem, block.block_id], "kind": "table",
                                           "model": getattr(reader, "model", ""),
                                           "payload_key": getattr(reader, "payload_key", "rows"),
                                           "request": make(parts, instruction)})
                        with table_lock:
                            with open(args.batch_prepare, "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                                fh.write(line + "\n")
                        return stem, block, None, {"error": "batched: queued"}
                for attempt in range(3):
                    try:
                        rows, usage = reader(parts, instruction)
                        if hit is not None:
                            tmp = hit.with_suffix(".json.part")
                            tmp.write_text(json.dumps({"lines": rows, "usage": usage,
                                                       "slot": [stem, block.block_id],
                                                       "kind": "table",
                                                       "model": getattr(reader, "model", ""),
                                                       "at": time.time()}), encoding="utf-8")
                            tmp.replace(hit)
                        return stem, block, rows, usage
                    except Truncated:
                        # Not a transient fault: the same call will truncate again
                        # at the same cap. Raise the ceiling instead of sleeping.
                        if hasattr(reader, "max_tokens"):
                            reader.max_tokens = min(reader.max_tokens * 2, 32000)
                        if attempt == 2:
                            return stem, block, None, {"error": "truncated"}
                    except Exception as exc:            # noqa: BLE001
                        if attempt == 2:
                            return stem, block, None, {"error": str(exc)}
                        time.sleep(2 * (attempt + 1))

            started = time.time()
            with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=args.workers) as pool:
                results = list(pool.map(run, targets))
            elapsed = time.time() - started

            failures = 0
            for stem, block, rows, usage in results:
                for key in ("input", "output", "cache_write", "cache_read"):
                    usage_total[key] += usage.get(key, 0)
                if rows is None:
                    failures += 1
                    continue
                a_raw[block.block_id] = rows
                rebuilt = rows_to_block(stem, block.index, rows)
                if rebuilt is None:
                    failures += 1
                    continue
                a_blocks[block.block_id] = rebuilt
                for record in lx.grade_page([rebuilt]):
                    record["channel"] = "A"
                    record["block_id"] = block.block_id
                    records.append(record)
            print(f"  {len(a_blocks)} blocks transcribed, {failures} failed, "
                  f"{elapsed:.0f}s wall clock "
                  f"({elapsed / max(len(targets), 1):.1f}s/block)")
            print(f"  tokens: {usage_total['input']:,} in "
                  f"({usage_total['cache_read']:,} cache reads), "
                  f"{usage_total['output']:,} out")
            if args.reader == "claude":
                cost = (usage_total["input"] * rate_in
                        + usage_total["cache_write"] * rate_in * 1.25
                        + usage_total["cache_read"] * rate_in * 0.1
                        + usage_total["output"] * rate_out) / 1e6
            elif reader_price:
                # No caching on this path, so every token billed at the full input
                # rate — which is why a cheaper per-token rate need not be cheaper
                # per block.
                cost = (usage_total["input"] * reader_price[0]
                        + usage_total["output"] * reader_price[1]) / 1e6
            else:
                cost = None
            if cost is None:
                print("  cost: not priced — pass --reader-price IN,OUT to put this "
                      "reader on the same yardstick (a self-hosted reader is priced "
                      "by whoever runs it; compare on the pass rate and s/block)")
            else:
                per_block = cost / max(len(a_blocks), 1)
                print(f"  cost: ${cost:.2f}  (${per_block:.4f}/block, "
                      f"${per_block * volume_blocks:,.0f} for the volume)")
                if args.reader == "claude":
                    print(f"        ${per_block * volume_blocks / 2:,.0f} on the Batches API "
                          f"(50% off, no latency guarantee)")
                elif usage_total["input"]:
                    # The system prompt is resent in full on every block here. Say
                    # how much of the bill that is, since it is the part prompt
                    # caching would have removed.
                    print(f"        no prompt caching on this path: "
                          f"{usage_total['input']:,} input tokens billed in full")

            for block_id, rebuilt in a_blocks.items():
                stem = block_id.split("#")[0]
                original = next(b for b in blocks_by_page[stem]
                                if b.block_id == block_id)
                for finding in compare_channels(original, rebuilt, "AB_agree"):
                    finding["channel"] = "A|B"
                    records.append(finding)

    # ---- channel C ------------------------------------------------------- #
    if "C" in channels:          # free — runs under --dry-run too
        print("\nchannel C (German volume) ...")
        try:
            import pandas as pd
            import pdfplumber

            districts = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data" / "final" / "geo" / "districts_1910.csv")
            index = lxde.build_page_index(DE_TEXT)
            pdf = pdfplumber.open(DE_PDF)

            # Pair through the authority, not by comparing the two volumes' names
            # to each other: both sides are OCR, and the German scan is the worse of
            # the two ("Uo.jeschin" for Hojeschin). Each side is matched to a known
            # obec instead, and two blocks are the same municipality when they
            # anchored to the same one.
            okres_id_to_de = {}
            for row in districts.itertuples():
                code = str(row.okres_code)
                if "-" in code:
                    land_code, number = code.split("-")
                    okres_id_to_de[int(f"{land_code}{int(number):03d}")] = str(row.okres_de)

            grid = lxde.fit_grid(pdf, list(range(60, 260)))
            findings: list[dict] = []
            paired_total = 0
            de_anchor_rows: list[dict] = []
            for okres_id, anchors in sorted(cz_anchors.items()):
                okres_de = okres_id_to_de.get(okres_id)
                de_pages = lxde.okres_pages(index, okres_de) if okres_de else []
                if not de_pages:
                    print(f"  okres {okres_id} ({okres_de}): "
                          f"not located in the German volume")
                    continue
                german_blocks: list[lx.Block] = []
                for number in de_pages:
                    rows = lxde.extract_rows_de(pdf, number, grid)
                    blocks, _ = lx.segment_blocks(rows)
                    german_blocks += [b for b in blocks if not lxde.is_heading(b)]
                candidates = authority.okres(okres_id)
                de_anchors = lxnm.anchor_blocks(german_blocks, candidates)
                pairs = lxnm.pair_by_obec(anchors, de_anchors)
                paired_total += len(pairs)
                matched_de = sum(1 for a in de_anchors if a.verdict == "matched")
                print(f"  {okres_de}: German pages {de_pages}, "
                      f"{len(german_blocks)} de blocks, {matched_de} anchored, "
                      f"{len(pairs)} paired with a Czech block")
                for anchor in de_anchors:
                    de_anchor_rows.append({
                        "block_id": anchor.block_id, "okres_id": okres_id,
                        "printed_name": anchor.printed, "verdict": anchor.verdict,
                        "obec": anchor.obec.cs_name if anchor.obec else "",
                        "score": anchor.score, "runner_up": anchor.runner_up,
                    })
                cz_by_id = {b.block_id: b for bs in blocks_by_page.values()
                            for b in bs}
                de_by_id = {b.block_id: b for b in german_blocks}
                for obec, cz_anchor, de_anchor in pairs:
                    cz_block = cz_by_id.get(cz_anchor.block_id)
                    de_block = de_by_id.get(de_anchor.block_id)
                    if cz_block is None or de_block is None:
                        continue
                    for finding in lxde.compare_cells(cz_block, de_block):
                        finding["row_name"] = obec.cs_name
                        findings.append(finding)
            for finding in findings:
                finding["channel"] = "C|B"
            records += findings
            write_csv(out_dir / "anchors_de.csv", de_anchor_rows)
            print(lxde.lexikon_1910_de_report(grid, paired_total, findings))
        except Exception as exc:                        # noqa: BLE001
            print(f"  channel C failed: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")

    # ---- report ---------------------------------------------------------- #
    # Labelled with the pass, for the same reason its other artefacts are: two
    # readers over the same pages must not overwrite each other's ledger.
    checks_name = f"checks_{args.notes_label}.csv" if args.notes_label else "checks.csv"
    write_csv(out_dir / checks_name, records)
    rows_name = (f"table_rows_{args.notes_label}.csv" if args.notes_label
                 else "table_rows.csv")
    write_csv(out_dir / rows_name, table_rows(blocks_by_page, a_raw))
    print()
    for channel in ("B", "A"):
        subset = [r for r in records if r.get("channel") == channel]
        if subset:
            print(f"--- channel {channel} against the invariants "
                  f"({len(blocks_by_page) if channel == 'B' else len(a_blocks)} "
                  f"pages/blocks)")
            print(lx.lexikon_1910_report(subset))
            print()
    for label, title in (("A|B", "channel A vs channel B"),
                         ("C|B", "channel C vs channel B")):
        subset = [r for r in records if r.get("channel") == label]
        if subset:
            counts = Counter(r["verdict"] for r in subset)
            graded = counts["pass"] + counts["fail"] + counts["unparseable"]
            rate = f"{counts['pass'] / graded:.1%}" if graded else "--"
            print(f"--- {title}: {counts['pass']} agree, {counts['fail']} disagree, "
                  f"{counts['unparseable']} unreadable, {counts['na']} both blank "
                  f"-> {rate} agreement")
    print(f"\nper-check records written to {out_dir / checks_name}")
    print(f"per-page geometry written to {out_dir / 'geometry.csv'}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
